title: Odyssey, Book 1
author: Homer
source_notes: Greek text: Monro & Allen via Perseus. English: Samuel Butler 1900 via Perseus.
reading_notes: Book 1 of the Odyssey. 444 lines. Per-line greek with per-line gloss; Samuel Butler's prose translation provided as parallel panel for context.

lines.original: ἄνδρα μοι ἔννεπε, μοῦσα, πολύτροπον, ὃς μάλα πολλὰ
lines.english: Tell me, Muse, of the man of many ways, who wandered very much
lines.gloss: **ἄνδρα** (acc. sing. masc. of ἀνήρ) "man, hero" – direct object of ἔννεπε; **ἔννεπε** (2nd sing. aor. imper. of ἐνέπω) "tell, relate" – imperative commanding the Muse; **μοῦσα** (voc. sing. fem.) "Muse" – goddess of poetry invoked; **πολύτροπον** (acc. sing. masc. of πολύτροπος) "much-turned, of many ways, versatile" – epithet modifying ἄνδρα; **πολλὰ** (acc. pl. neut. of πολύς) "many things" – direct object of πλάγχθη in the next line. The famous opening invokes the Muse to sing of

lines.original: πλάγχθη, ἐπεὶ Τροίης ἱερὸν πτολίεθρον ἔπερσεν·
lines.english: He wandered far after he sacked the sacred citadel of Troy.
lines.gloss: **πλάγχθη** (aorist passive indicative, 3rd singular, from πλάζω): "he was driven off course, wandered" – the verb governing the opening sentence's subject, describing Odysseus's protracted travels. **ἐπεί**: temporal conjunction, "after, since." **Τροίης**: genitive singular of Τροία, "of Troy," dependent on πτολίεθρον. **πτολίεθρον**: accusative singular neuter noun, "citadel, city" (poetic equivalent of πόλις). **ἔπερσεν**: aorist active indicative, 3rd singular, from πέρθω, "he sacked, destroyed."

lines.original: πολλῶν δʼ ἀνθρώπων ἴδεν ἄστεα καὶ νόον ἔγνω,
lines.english: He saw the cities of many peoples and came to know their minds.
lines.gloss: **πολλῶν** (adj., gen. pl. masc. of πολύς): "of many," modifying ἀνθρώπων. **ἀνθρώπων** (noun, gen. pl. of ἄνθρωπος): "of men/people," depending on ἄστεα and νόον. **ἴδεν** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. indic. of ὁράω): "he saw." **ἄστεα** (noun, acc. pl. of ἄστυ): "cities." **ἔγνω** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. indic. of γιγνώσκω): "he came to know." The hero saw the cities of many peoples and learned their mind/character, emphasizing his wanderings and cultural experience.

lines.original: πολλὰ δʼ ὅ γʼ ἐν πόντῳ πάθεν ἄλγεα ὃν κατὰ θυμόν,
lines.english: Many sufferings he endured on the sea in his heart.
lines.gloss: **πολλά** (adj., neut. acc. pl.) "many things" — direct object of **πάθεν** (aorist 3rd sg. of πάσχω) "he suffered." **πόντῳ** (noun, masc. dat. sg.) "on the sea" — locative dative. **ἄλγεα** (noun, neut. acc. pl.) "pains, griefs" — in apposition to πολλά. **θυμόν** (noun, masc. acc. sg.) "heart, spirit" — with κατά forms adverbial phrase "in his heart/spirit." The line emphasizes Odysseus's extensive suffering at sea, both external and internal.

lines.original: ἀρνύμενος ἥν τε ψυχὴν καὶ νόστον ἑταίρων.
lines.english: striving to win his own life and the homecoming of his companions.
lines.gloss: **ἀρνύμενος** (pres. mid. ptc. nom. sg. masc., *ἄρνυμαι*) "striving to win, trying to secure"; **ψυχήν** (acc. sg. fem., *ψυχή*) "life, soul"; **νόστον** (acc. sg. masc., *νόστος*) "return, homecoming"; **ἑταίρων** (gen. pl. masc., *ἑταῖρος*) "of companions." The line describes Odysseus striving to win both his own life and the homecoming of his companions, with the genitive objective indicating whose return he sought.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδʼ ὣς ἑτάρους ἐρρύσατο, ἱέμενός περ·
lines.english: But not even so did he save his companions, though he longed to.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλʼ οὐδʼ ὣς ἑτάρους ἐρρύσατο, ἱέμενός περ·**

*ἀλλά* (conjunction): "but, yet"; *οὐδέ* (negative conjunction): "not even"; *ὥς* (adverb): "thus, in this way"; *ἑτάρους* (noun, acc. pl. masc.): "companions"; *ἐρρύσατο* (verb, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ῥύομαι): "he saved, rescued"; *ἱέμενός* (participle, nom. sg. masc. pres. mid. of ἵημι): "striving, desiring"; *περ* (particle): "although, even." Despite his striving,

lines.original: αὐτῶν γὰρ σφετέρῃσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν ὄλοντο,
lines.english: For by their own recklessness they perished,
lines.gloss:
**αὐτῶν** (pronoun, genitive plural masculine of αὐτός): "by their own" (intensive, emphasizing possession).
**σφετέρῃσιν** (adjective, dative plural feminine of σφέτερος): "by their own" (possessive, reinforcing αὐτῶν).
**ἀτασθαλίῃσιν** (noun, dative plural of ἀτασθαλίη): "by recklessness/folly" (instrumental dative).
**ὄλοντο** (verb, 3rd plural aorist middle indicative of ὄλλυμι): "they perished."

The companions perished through their own reckless folly, with the doubled possessive (αὐτῶν...σφετέρῃσιν) emphasizing personal responsibility for their destruction.

lines.original: νήπιοι, οἳ κατὰ βοῦς Ὑπερίονος Ἠελίοιο
lines.english: The fools, who devoured the cattle of Hyperion Helios.
lines.gloss:
**νήπιοι** (nom. pl. masc., adjective): "fools" or "childish ones" – appositive to the implied subject, expressing moral censure. **κατὰ** (preposition + acc.): "down" or "utterly," here intensifying the verb (tmesis with κατ-έφαγον understood). **βοῦς** (acc. pl., βοῦς): "cattle," direct object. **Ὑπερίονος** (gen. sg., Ὑπερίων): "of Hyperion," patronymic. **Ἠελίοιο** (gen. sg., Ἠέλιος): "of Helios/the Sun-god," in apposition to Ὑπερίονος, specifying whose cattle were devoured.

The line condemns the companions as fools who ate the cattle of Helios

lines.original: ἤσθιον· αὐτὰρ ὁ τοῖσιν ἀφείλετο νόστιμον ἦμαρ.
lines.english: They ate them, and he took away from them the day of their homecoming.
lines.gloss:
**ἤσθιον** (imperf. 3rd pl. of ἔδω): "they ate/were eating" – describes the crew's consumption of the cattle. **αὐτάρ** (particle): "but, and" – marks a strong transition to the consequence. **ἀφείλετο** (aor. mid. 3rd sg. of ἀφαιρέω): "he took away" – Helios deprived them. **νόστιμον** (adj. acc. sg. neut.): "of return, homecoming" – modifies ἦμαρ. **ἦμαρ** (noun acc. sg. neut.): "day" – the day of return, metonymy for the return itself.

The line explains that the crew ate the cattle, but Helios therefore took away their day of homecoming (i.e., they never returned home).

lines.original: τῶν ἁμόθεν γε, θεά, θύγατερ Διός, εἰπὲ καὶ ἡμῖν.
lines.english: Of these things tell us now, goddess, daughter of Zeus, beginning from some point.
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (demonstrative genitive plural): "of these things," referring to the events mentioned; **ἁμόθεν** (adverb): "from some point," indicating starting place in the narrative; **θύγατερ** (vocative singular of θυγάτηρ): "daughter," in apposition to θεά; **εἰπὲ** (aorist imperative, 2nd singular of εἶπον/λέγω): "tell," the poet's invocation to the Muse. The line invokes the Muse, daughter of Zeus, to narrate some part of these events to the poet.

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ἄλλοι μὲν πάντες, ὅσοι φύγον αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον,
lines.english: Then all the others, as many as had escaped sheer destruction, were at home having fled both war and sea.
lines.gloss:
**ἔνθʼ** (ἔνθα): adverb, "then" or "at that time" (temporal use)
**φύγον**: 3rd plural aorist active indicative of φεύγω, "escaped" or "fled"
**αἰπὺν**: accusative singular masculine adjective, "sheer" or "steep" (metaphorically "utter")
**ὄλεθρον**: accusative singular masculine noun, "destruction" or "death"

The line describes "all the others who escaped sheer destruction," marking a temporal transition with ἔνθα and using the aorist φύγον to indicate completed action.

lines.original: οἴκοι ἔσαν, πόλεμόν τε πεφευγότες ἠδὲ θάλασσαν·
lines.english: were at home, having escaped both war and sea
lines.gloss:
**οἴκοι** (adverb): "at home," locative form indicating place where the other survivors were safe.

**πεφευγότες** (perfect active participle, nominative plural masculine, from φεύγω): "having escaped/fled," describing those who survived both war and sea.

**πόλεμόν τε...ἠδὲ θάλασσαν** (accusative objects): "both war and sea," the twin perils from which all others had escaped, connected by τε...ἠδέ correlatives.

The line establishes the contrast: all other Greeks were safely home, having survived the dual dangers of the Trojan War and the perilous sea voyage.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ οἶον νόστου κεχρημένον ἠδὲ γυναικὸς
lines.english: But him alone, longing for his homecoming and his wife,
lines.gloss:
**τὸν** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular masculine): "him," referring to Odysseus alone among the heroes.

**οἶον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine): "alone," emphasizing his isolation.

**νόστου** (noun, genitive singular): "of homecoming/return," object of desire with κεχρημένον.

**κεχρημένον** (perfect middle/passive participle, accusative singular masculine, from χρή/χράομαι): "desiring, longing for," governing the genitives νόστου and γυναικός.

**γυναικός** (noun, genitive singular): "of his wife" (Penelope), paired with νόστου as dual objects of longing.

The line contrasts Odysseus's solitary state with his twin yearnings for homecoming and his wife, while the nymph Calypso detains him.

lines.original: νύμφη πότνιʼ ἔρυκε Καλυψὼ δῖα θεάων
lines.english: The nymph, queenly Calypso, divine among goddesses, detained him in her hollow caves.
lines.gloss:
**νύμφη** (nom. sg. fem., "nymph") **πότνιʼ** (< πότνια, voc. sg. fem., "mistress, lady") **ἔρυκε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἐρύκω, "was detaining, holding back") **Καλυψώ** (nom. sg., "Calypso") **θεάων** (gen. pl. fem., θεά, "of goddesses"). 

The nymph-mistress Calypso, divine among goddesses, was detaining him; the line emphasizes Odysseus's captivity through the compound epithets for his captor.

lines.original: ἐν σπέσσι γλαφυροῖσι, λιλαιομένη πόσιν εἶναι.
lines.english: in her hollow caves, desiring him to be her husband.
lines.gloss: In **ἐν σπέσσι γλαφυροῖσι** (dative plural, "in hollow caves"), the adjective *γλαφυροῖσι* modifies the location where Calypso detained Odysseus. **λιλαιομένη** (present middle participle, nominative feminine singular, "desiring/longing") describes Calypso's state, while **πόσιν** (accusative singular, "husband") serves as the object of her desire with **εἶναι** (present infinitive, "to be") completing the indirect statement: "she longing [for him] to be [her] husband."

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅτε δὴ ἔτος ἦλθε περιπλομένων ἐνιαυτῶν,
lines.english: But when the year came in the cycle of revolving seasons,
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλ' ὅτε δὴ ἔτος ἦλθε περιπλομένων ἐνιαυτῶν**

**ὅτε** (conjunction) "when"; **ἔτος** (noun, nom. sg. neut.) "year"; **ἦλθε** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. indic. from ἔρχομαι) "came"; **περιπλομένων** (participle, gen. pl. pres. mid. from περιπέλομαι) "revolving, rolling round"; **ἐνιαυτῶν** (noun, gen. pl. masc.) "of years." This verse marks the completion of a fated cycle: "But when the year came in the revolving of years."

lines.original: τῷ οἱ ἐπεκλώσαντο θεοὶ οἶκόνδε νέεσθαι
lines.english: in which the gods had spun for him his return homeward
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἐπεκλώσαντο (verb, 3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of ἐπικλώθω, "they spun out, allotted"), θεοί (noun, nom. pl., "gods"), οἶκόνδε (adverb, "homeward"), νέεσθαι (verb, pres. mid. inf. of νέομαι, "to return, go"). 

The gods allotted/destined for him (Odysseus) to return home, with ἐπικλώθω evoking the Fates' spinning of destiny.

lines.original: εἰς Ἰθάκην, οὐδʼ ἔνθα πεφυγμένος ἦεν ἀέθλων
lines.english: to Ithaca, nor even there had he escaped from struggles
lines.gloss:
**εἰς Ἰθάκην, οὐδʼ ἔνθα πεφυγμένος ἦεν ἀέθλων**

*εἰς* (preposition + acc.): "to, into" — *Ἰθάκην* (acc. sg.): Ithaca, Odysseus's homeland. *πεφυγμένος* (perf. mid./pass. part., nom. sg. masc.): "having escaped, being free from." *ἦεν* (3rd sg. imperf.): "he was" (= ἦν). *ἀέθλων* (gen. pl.): "from labors, contests, struggles." Even upon returning to Ithaca, Odysseus was not free from toils—foreshadowing the suitors' challenge.

lines.original: καὶ μετὰ οἷσι φίλοισι. θεοὶ δʼ ἐλέαιρον ἅπαντες
lines.english: even among his own dear ones, and all the gods pitied him
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** φίλοισι (φίλος, -η, -ον): dative plural masculine adjective, "dear ones, companions"; θεοὶ (θεός, -οῦ, ὁ): nominative plural, "the gods"; ἐλέαιρον (ἐλεαίρω): third plural imperfect active indicative, "they pitied"; ἅπαντες (ἅπας, ἅπασα, ἅπαν): nominative plural masculine adjective, "all."

The line completes the thought "even among his dear ones" and introduces divine pity: all the gods took pity (on Odysseus), setting up the exception of Poseidon in the next verse.

lines.original: νόσφι Ποσειδάωνος· ὁ δʼ ἀσπερχὲς μενέαινεν
lines.english: except Poseidon, who relentlessly raged on
lines.gloss: **νόσφι** (adverb): "apart from, without"; governs genitive **Ποσειδάωνος** (masculine genitive singular): "Poseidon" — all the gods pitied Odysseus except Poseidon. **ὁ δʼ** (masculine nominative singular demonstrative pronoun): "but he" refers to Poseidon. **ἀσπερχὲς** (neuter accusative singular adverb): "unceasingly, relentlessly." **μενέαινεν** (third singular imperfect active indicative of μενεαίνω): "he raged, was wroth" — Poseidon continued his relentless anger against godlike Odysseus.

lines.original: ἀντιθέῳ Ὀδυσῆι πάρος ἣν γαῖαν ἱκέσθαι.
lines.english: against godlike Odysseus before he could reach his native land.
lines.gloss: **ἀντιθέῳ** (adj. dat. sg. masc.) "godlike," modifying Odysseus; **Ὀδυσῆι** (noun, dat. sg.) "for/against Odysseus," dative of disadvantage; **πάρος** (adv.) "before"; **γαῖαν** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "land," object of the infinitive; **ἱκέσθαι** (verb, aor. inf. mid.) "to reach, arrive at." Poseidon raged relentlessly against godlike Odysseus before he could reach his homeland.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὁ μὲν Αἰθίοπας μετεκίαθε τηλόθʼ ἐόντας,
lines.english: But he had gone to visit the Ethiopians who dwell afar,
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλʼ ὁ μὲν Αἰθίοπας μετεκίαθε τηλόθʼ ἐόντας**

Key words: **ἀλλά** (conjunction) "but"; **ὁ μέν** (pronoun, nom. sg.) "he" (on the one hand, beginning a μέν...δέ construction); **Αἰθίοπας** (noun, acc. pl.) "Ethiopians"; **μετεκίαθε** (verb, 3rd sg. pluperfect middle) "had gone to visit"; **τηλόθʼ ἐόντας** (adverb + participle, acc. pl.) "being far away." This line explains Poseidon's absence from the divine council—he had gone to the distant Ethiopians.

lines.original: Αἰθίοπας τοὶ διχθὰ δεδαίαται, ἔσχατοι ἀνδρῶν,
lines.english: The Ethiopians who are divided in two, the most remote of men,
lines.gloss: **Αἰθίοπας** (acc. pl., "Ethiopians") **τοὶ** (nom. pl. relative pronoun, "who") **διχθὰ** (adverb, "in two parts, asunder") **δεδαίαται** (3rd sg. perfect mid./pass., *δαίω*, "are divided") **ἔσχατοι** (nom. pl. adj., "farthest, remotest") **ἀνδρῶν** (gen. pl., "of men"). The Ethiopians, who are divided in two parts and are the most remote of mortals—a parenthetical elaboration explaining their geography before the next line specifies their eastward and westward divisions.

lines.original: οἱ μὲν δυσομένου Ὑπερίονος οἱ δʼ ἀνιόντος,
lines.english: Some where the sun sets and others where it rises.
lines.gloss:
**οἱ μέν** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine): "some" or "the one group" (first part of correlative construction with οἱ δέ).

**δυσομένου** (present middle participle, genitive singular masculine, from δύω): "of the setting" (modifying Ὑπερίονος).

**Ὑπερίονος** (proper noun, genitive singular): "of Hyperion" (i.e., the Sun).

**οἱ δέ** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine): "and others" or "the other group" (completing the correlative construction).

**ἀνιόντος** (present active participle, genitive singular masculine, from ἄνειμι): "of the rising" (also modifying Ὑπερίονος understood).

The line describes the Ethiopians divided

lines.original: ἀντιόων ταύρων τε καὶ ἀρνειῶν ἑκατόμβης.
lines.english: looking to receive hecatombs of bulls and rams.
lines.gloss: **ἀντιόων** (pres. act. participle, gen. pl. masc. of ἀντιάω) "encountering, partaking of"; **ταύρων** (gen. pl. of ταῦρος) "of bulls"; **ἀρνειῶν** (gen. pl. of ἀρνειός) "of rams"; **ἑκατόμβης** (gen. sg. of ἑκατόμβη) "of the hecatomb, sacrificial offering." The line describes participants feasting on a sacrifice consisting of bulls and rams, with the genitive participle construction indicating their partaking of the hecatomb.

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ὅ γʼ ἐτέρπετο δαιτὶ παρήμενος· οἱ δὲ δὴ ἄλλοι
lines.english: There he took pleasure in the feast sitting beside them, but the other gods
lines.gloss: **ἔνθʼ** (adverb): "there," referring to the location in Zeus's halls. **ἐτέρπετο** (3rd sg. imperf. mid. ind., *τέρπω*): "he was taking pleasure" or "he was enjoying himself." **δαιτί** (dat. sg. fem., *δαίς*): "in the feast," dative of means/respect. **παρήμενος** (nom. sg. masc. perf. mid. ptc., *πάρειμι*): "sitting beside" or "being present at." The line describes how he (likely a god) was enjoying the feast while seated there, contrasting with "the others" (*οἱ δὲ δὴ ἄλλοι*) who will be mentioned next.

lines.original: Ζηνὸς ἐνὶ μεγάροισιν Ὀλυμπίου ἁθρόοι ἦσαν.
lines.english: The others were gathered together in the halls of Olympian Zeus.
lines.gloss:
**Ζηνὸς** (gen. sg. of Ζεύς): "of Zeus," indicating possession of the halls. **μεγάροισιν** (dat. pl. of μέγαρον): "in the halls/palace," locative dative. **Ὀλυμπίου** (gen. sg. of Ὀλύμπιος): "Olympian," epithet modifying Zeus. **ἁθρόοι** (nom. pl. masc. of ἁθρόος): "assembled together," predicate adjective. **ἦσαν** (3rd pl. imperf. of εἰμί): "they were." 

The gods were gathered together in the halls of Olympian Zeus, setting the scene for the divine council.

lines.original: τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε·
lines.english: Among them the father of men and gods began to speak.
lines.gloss:
**Line:** τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε·

**Gloss:** τοῖσι (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural) "to them/among them"; μύθων (noun, genitive plural) "of words/speech"; ἦρχε (verb, 3rd sg. imperfect active) "began" (+ genitive); πατὴρ (noun, nominative singular) "father"; ἀνδρῶν...θεῶν (genitive plural nouns) "of men...of gods." Zeus, father of gods and men, began speaking among the assembled Olympians.

lines.original: μνήσατο γὰρ κατὰ θυμὸν ἀμύμονος Αἰγίσθοιο,
lines.english: For he remembered in his heart blameless Aigisthos.
lines.gloss:
**μνήσατο** (verb, 3rd sg. aorist middle indicative of μιμνῄσκομαι): "he remembered, called to mind"
**κατὰ θυμόν** (prepositional phrase): "in his heart/mind," an idiomatic expression for internal thought
**ἀμύμονος** (adjective, genitive sg. masculine): "blameless, noble" (ironic epithet)
**Αἰγίσθοιο** (proper noun, genitive sg.): "of Aegisthus," the adulterer slain by Orestes

Zeus remembered in his heart noble Aegisthus, whose death at Orestes' hands will frame the poem's meditation on homecoming and justice.

lines.original: τόν ῥʼ Ἀγαμεμνονίδης τηλεκλυτὸς ἔκτανʼ Ὀρέστης·
lines.english: whom far-famed Orestes, the son of Agamemnon, slew.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Odyssey 1.30:**

*τόν* (demonstrative pronoun, masculine accusative singular) refers back to Aegisthus; *Ἀγαμεμνονίδης* (patronymic nominative singular) "son of Agamemnon," i.e., Orestes; *τηλεκλυτός* (adjective nominative singular) "far-famed, renowned"; *ἔκτανε(ν)* (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular, κτείνω) "killed, slew." Zeus recalls how the famous Orestes, son of Agamemnon, killed Aegisthus in vengeance.

lines.original: τοῦ ὅ γʼ ἐπιμνησθεὶς ἔπεʼ ἀθανάτοισι μετηύδα·
lines.english: Remembering him, he spoke these words among the immortals.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 
- **τοῦ** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive singular masculine): "of him/that," referring to Orestes/Aegisthus from the previous line
- **ἐπιμνησθεὶς** (aorist middle participle, nominative singular masculine, from ἐπιμιμνῄσκομαι): "remembering, calling to mind"
- **ἔπεα** (noun, accusative plural neuter, from ἔπος): "words, speech"
- **ἀθανάτοισι** (adjective used as noun, dative plural masculine/feminine): "to the immortals, to the gods"
- **μετηύδα** (imperfect active, 3rd singular, from μεταυδάω): "he spoke, addressed"

Zeus, remembering the Orestes exemplum, spoke words

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἠμείβετʼ ἔπειτα θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: Then the goddess, grey-eyed Athena, answered him in turn.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Odyssey line: τὸν δʼ ἠμείβετʼ ἔπειτα θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·**

**ἠμείβετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ἀμείβω): "answered, replied to" (him). **ἔπειτα** (adv.): "then, thereupon." **θεά** (nom. sg. fem.): "the goddess." **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. epithet): "grey-eyed, bright-eyed." **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg.): "Athena." 

Then the goddess, grey-eyed Athena, answered him in reply.

lines.original: τὴν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς·
lines.english: Answering her in turn, Zeus the cloud-gatherer spoke:
lines.gloss:
**τὴν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς·**

**ἀπαμειβόμενος**: present middle participle, nominative singular masculine of ἀπαμείβομαι, "answering (in return)." **προσέφη**: 3rd singular aorist indicative active of προσφημί, "he addressed, spoke to." **νεφεληγερέτα**: nominative singular masculine epithet (compound adjective), "cloud-gathering," modifying Zeus. **Ζεύς**: nominative singular, "Zeus" (subject). Zeus, the cloud-gatherer, answering her in turn, addressed (Athena).

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἠμείβετʼ ἔπειτα θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: Then the goddess, bright-eyed Athena, answered him in turn.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἠμείβετʼ (ἀμείβομαι, 3rd sg. impf. mid., "answered"), θεά (nom. sg., "goddess"), γλαυκῶπις (nom. sg. epithet, "grey-eyed/bright-eyed"), Ἀθήνη (nom. sg., "Athena").

Then the goddess, grey-eyed Athena, answered him in turn. The verb ἠμείβετο governs the accusative τόν ("him"), referring back to Zeus from the previous line.

lines.original: ὣς εἰποῦσʼ ὑπὸ ποσσὶν ἐδήσατο καλὰ πέδιλα,
lines.english: So speaking, she bound the beautiful sandals beneath her feet.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς εἰποῦσʼ ὑπὸ ποσσὶν ἐδήσατο καλὰ πέδιλα**

*εἰποῦσα* (aorist participle, feminine nominative singular of *εἶπον*, "having spoken"); *ποσσίν* (dative plural of *πούς*, "feet," here "under her feet"); *ἐδήσατο* (aorist middle indicative, 3rd singular of *δέω*, "she bound for herself"); *πέδιλα* (accusative plural neuter, "sandals"). Athena, having spoken thus, bound her beautiful sandals under her feet, preparing for divine travel.

lines.original: ἀμβρόσια χρύσεια, τά μιν φέρον ἠμὲν ἐφʼ ὑγρὴν
lines.english: immortal golden sandals that carried her over the wet sea and the boundless earth as swift as the wind's breath
lines.gloss: **ἀμβρόσια** (adj. nom. pl. neut.) "immortal, divine" - modifies πέδιλα from the previous line; **χρύσεια** (adj. nom. pl. neut.) "golden" - also modifies πέδιλα; **τά** (rel. pron. nom. pl. neut.) "which" - introduces a relative clause referring to the sandals; **μιν** (pron. acc. sg.) "him/her" (here "her," referring to Athena); **φέρον** (imperf. act. ind. 3rd pl.) "were carrying"; **ὑγρήν** (adj. acc. sg. fem.) "wet, watery" - likely modifying an understood noun like "sea." The golden immortal sandals carry Athena over both the wet sea and the boundless earth.

lines.original: ἠδʼ ἐπʼ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν ἅμα πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο·
lines.english: and over the boundless earth together with the blasts of the wind
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 

- **ἠδʼ** (ἠδέ): conjunction, "and, and also"
- **ἀπείρονα**: adjective, accusative feminine singular (modifying γαῖαν), "boundless, infinite"
- **γαῖαν**: noun, accusative singular, "land, earth"
- **πνοιῇς**: noun, dative singular (from πνοιή), "blast, breath"
- **ἀνέμοιο**: noun, genitive singular, "of the wind"

This line completes the description of Hermes' golden sandals carrying him over both the sea (ὑγρήν from the previous line) and the boundless earth as swiftly as the wind's blast.

lines.original: εἵλετο δʼ ἄλκιμον ἔγχος, ἀκαχμένον ὀξέι χαλκῷ,
lines.english: He took a mighty spear, pointed with sharp bronze.
lines.gloss: **εἵλετο** (aorist middle, 3rd sg. of αἱρέω) "he took"; **ἄλκιμον** (adj. acc. sg. neut.) "strong, mighty"; **ἔγχος** (noun acc. sg. neut.) "spear"; **ἀκαχμένον** (perfect passive participle acc. sg. neut. of ἀκάζω) "pointed, sharpened"; **ὀξέι** (adj. dat. sg. masc./neut.) "sharp"; **χαλκῷ** (noun dat. sg. masc.) "bronze." The hero took a mighty spear, one sharpened with sharp bronze.

lines.original: βριθὺ μέγα στιβαρόν, τῷ δάμνησι στίχας ἀνδρῶν
lines.english: heavy great massive with which he subdues the ranks of men
lines.gloss:
**βριθὺ** (adj., nom. neut. sg.) "heavy"; **μέγα** (adj., nom. neut. sg.) "great, large"; **στιβαρόν** (adj., nom. neut. sg.) "stout, sturdy"; **δάμνησι** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. subj. act.) "he subdues, overpowers"; **στίχας** (noun, acc. pl.) "ranks, rows." 

The line describes the spear as heavy, large, and sturdy, with which he (Athena disguised as a warrior) subdues ranks of men—emphasizing the formidable nature of the weapon wielded by one of divine strength or lineage.

lines.original: ἡρώων, τοῖσίν τε κοτέσσεται ὀβριμοπάτρη.
lines.english: of heroes, with whom the mighty-fathered one grows angry.
lines.gloss:
**ἡρώων** (gen. pl. of ἥρως): "of heroes," dependent on στίχας ἀνδρῶν from the previous line. **τοῖσίν** (dat. pl. relative pronoun): "against whom," indirect object of κοτέσσεται. **κοτέσσεται** (3rd sg. pres. mid. indic. of κοτέω): "is wrathful, bears anger." **ὀβριμοπάτρη** (nom. sg. fem. adj.): "she of the mighty father," a compound epithet describing Athena in apposition to the subject of κοτέσσεται.

This line completes the description of Athena's spear with which she subdues ranks of heroic warriors whenever she, daughter of the mighty father, is angered against them.

lines.original: βῆ δὲ κατʼ Οὐλύμποιο καρήνων ἀίξασα,
lines.english: She went darting down from the peaks of Olympus.
lines.gloss: **βῆ** (3rd sg. aor. of βαίνω) "she went"; **κατʼ** (κατά + gen.) "down from"; **Οὐλύμποιο** (gen. sg. of Ὄλυμπος) "Olympus"; **καρήνων** (gen. pl. of κάρηνον) "peaks, summits"; **ἀίξασα** (aor. part. fem. nom. sg. of ἀΐσσω) "darting, rushing." Athena descends swiftly from the peaks of Mount Olympus.

lines.original: στῆ δʼ Ἰθάκης ἐνὶ δήμῳ ἐπὶ προθύροις Ὀδυσῆος,
lines.english: She stood in the land of Ithaca at the doorway of Odysseus.
lines.gloss: **στῆ** (3rd sg. aorist act. indic. of ἵστημι) "she stood"; **Ἰθάκης** (gen. sg. fem.) "of Ithaca"; **δήμῳ** (dat. sg. masc.) "in the land/district"; **προθύροις** (dat. pl. neut.) "at the doorway/entrance"; **Ὀδυσῆος** (gen. sg. masc.) "of Odysseus." Athena arrives and takes her stand in Ithaca at the entrance of Odysseus's house.

lines.original: οὐδοῦ ἐπʼ αὐλείου· παλάμῃ δʼ ἔχε χάλκεον ἔγχος,
lines.english: upon the threshold of the court, and in her hand she held a bronze spear
lines.gloss:
**οὐδοῦ ἐπʼ αὐλείου· παλάμῃ δʼ ἔχε χάλκεον ἔγχος,**

*οὐδοῦ* (genitive of οὐδός): "of the threshold," describing location. *αὐλείου* (genitive adjective): "of the courtyard," modifying οὐδοῦ. *παλάμῃ* (dative of παλάμη): "in her hand," instrumental dative. *ἔχε* (3rd sg. imperfect of ἔχω): "she held." *χάλκεον* (neuter accusative adjective): "bronze," modifying ἔγχος. *ἔγχος* (neuter accusative noun): "spear," direct object. Athena

lines.original: εἰδομένη ξείνῳ, Ταφίων ἡγήτορι Μέντῃ.
lines.english: looking like a stranger, Mentes the leader of the Taphians.
lines.gloss:
**Target line:** εἰδομένη ξείνῳ, Ταφίων ἡγήτορι Μέντῃ.

**Key words:**
- **εἰδομένη**: perfect middle/passive participle, nominative singular feminine of εἴδομαι, "having made herself resemble" or "disguised as"
- **ξείνῳ**: noun, dative singular masculine of ξεῖνος, "guest-friend, stranger"
- **ἡγήτορι**: noun, dative singular masculine of ἡγήτωρ, "leader, chief"
- **Μέντῃ**: proper noun, dative singular of Μέντης, "Mentes"

Athena appears disguised as a guest-friend, specifically as Mentes, the leader of the Taphians, with the datives indicating the

lines.original: εὗρε δʼ ἄρα μνηστῆρας ἀγήνορας. οἱ μὲν ἔπειτα
lines.english: And she found the proud suitors, who then were amusing themselves with dice before the doors.
lines.gloss:
**εὗρε δʼ ἄρα μνηστῆρας ἀγήνορας. οἱ μὲν ἔπειτα**

**εὗρε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of εὑρίσκω): "she found"; **μνηστῆρας** (acc. pl. masc. of μνηστήρ): "the suitors"; **ἀγήνορας** (acc. pl. masc. of ἀγήνωρ): "proud, haughty"; **οἱ** (nom. pl. masc. article/demonstrative): "they"; **ἔπειτα** (adverb): "then, thereupon." Athena, disguised as Mentes, discovers the arrogant suitors, who are then described engaging in leisure

lines.original: πεσσοῖσι προπάροιθε θυράων θυμὸν ἔτερπον
lines.english: They were amusing themselves with dice in front of the doors.
lines.gloss:
**πεσσοῖσι** (dative plural of πεσσός) "with gaming pieces/draughts" – **προπάροιθε** (preposition + genitive) "before, in front of" – **θυράων** (genitive plural of θύρα) "of the doors" – **θυμὸν** (accusative singular of θυμός) "their spirit/heart" – **ἔτερπον** (3rd plural imperfect middle/passive of τέρπω) "they were delighting, amusing."

The suitors were entertaining themselves with board games in front of the doors, having just slaughtered cattle for their feast.

lines.original: ἥμενοι ἐν ῥινοῖσι βοῶν, οὓς ἔκτανον αὐτοί·
lines.english: seated on the hides of oxen which they themselves had slain
lines.gloss:
**ἥμενοι** (pres. mid./pass. ptc. nom. masc. pl. of ἧμαι) "sitting, seated"; **ἐν ῥινοῖσι** (prep. + dat. pl. of ῥινός) "on the hides"; **βοῶν** (gen. pl. of βοῦς) "of cattle/oxen"; **ἔκτανον** (aor. act. indic. 3rd pl. of κτείνω) "they slew/killed"; **αὐτοί** (nom. masc. pl. intensive pronoun) "themselves, they themselves." 

The suitors sat on the hides of cattle which they themselves had slaughtered, emphasizing their presumptuous consumption of Odysseus' livestock.

lines.original: κήρυκες δʼ αὐτοῖσι καὶ ὀτρηροὶ θεράποντες
lines.english: Heralds and eager attendants served them.
lines.gloss: **κήρυκες** (nom. pl., "heralds") **δʼ** (postpositive particle, "and/but") **αὐτοῖσι** (dat. pl. pronoun, "for them") **ὀτρηροὶ** (nom. pl. adj., "busy, active, swift") **θεράποντες** (nom. pl., "attendants, servants"). The heralds and busy attendants are the subject, serving the feasting suitors; **αὐτοῖσι** indicates the dative of advantage.

lines.original: οἱ μὲν οἶνον ἔμισγον ἐνὶ κρητῆρσι καὶ ὕδωρ,
lines.english: Some mixed wine and water in the mixing bowls.
lines.gloss: **οἱ μὲν** (article + particle): "some" or "the former," nominative plural masculine, indicating one group in a μὲν...δὲ construction. **οἶνον** (οἶνος): accusative singular masculine noun, "wine," direct object of ἔμισγον. **ἔμισγον** (μίγνυμι): 3rd person plural imperfect active indicative, "they were mixing" or "they mixed." **κρητῆρσι** (κρατήρ): dative plural masculine noun, "in mixing-bowls," indicating location where wine and water are combined. The line describes servants preparing wine by mixing it with water in large bowls, a standard Greek symposiastic practice.

lines.original: οἱ δʼ αὖτε σπόγγοισι πολυτρήτοισι τραπέζας
lines.english: Others wiped the tables with porous sponges.
lines.gloss:
**οἱ δʼ αὖτε** (nom. pl. masc. article + particle): "and they in turn"
**σπόγγοισι** (dat. pl. masc., σπόγγος): "with sponges," instrumental dative
**πολυτρήτοισι** (dat. pl. masc., adj.): "many-holed, full of holes," modifying σπόγγοισι
**τραπέζας** (acc. pl. fem., τράπεζα): "tables," direct object of an implied verb (wiping/cleaning)

The servants wipe down the tables with porous sponges as part of preparing the banquet, continuing the scene of meal preparation.

lines.original: νίζον καὶ πρότιθεν, τοὶ δὲ κρέα πολλὰ δατεῦντο.
lines.english: They washed the tables and set them out, and the others distributed abundant meat.
lines.gloss: **νίζον** (νίζω, 3rd pl. impf. act., "they washed") and **πρότιθεν** (προτίθημι, 3rd pl. impf. act., "they set forth") continue the servants' tasks of washing the tables and laying out food. **τοί** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. pl., "those [men]," i.e., the suitors) shifts focus to the diners. **κρέα** (κρέας, acc. pl. neut., "meats") and **δατεῦντο** (δατέομαι, 3rd pl. impf. mid., "divided among themselves") describe the suitors carving and distributing abundant portions of meat.

lines.original: τὴν δὲ πολὺ πρῶτος ἴδε Τηλέμαχος θεοειδής,
lines.english: Godlike Telemachos saw her first by far.
lines.gloss:
**τὴν δὲ πολὺ πρῶτος ἴδε Τηλέμαχος θεοειδής**

**τὴν** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular feminine): "her" (Athena in disguise as Mentes)
**πολὺ πρῶτος** (adverb + adjective, nominative singular masculine): "by far the first," "much the first" (intensive construction)
**ἴδε** (verb, 3rd singular aorist indicative active of ὁράω): "saw," "beheld"
**θεοειδής** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "godlike," "divine in appearance"

Godlike Telemachus saw her far before anyone else, as he sat among the suitors with his heart troubled.

lines.original: ἧστο γὰρ ἐν μνηστῆρσι φίλον τετιημένος ἦτορ,
lines.english: He sat among the suitors with his heart troubled, imagining his noble father might come from somewhere.
lines.gloss: ἧστο (ἧμαι): 3rd sg. pluperfect middle-passive, "he was sitting." μνηστῆρσι (μνηστήρ): dat. pl. masc., "among the suitors." τετιημένος (τείρω): perf. middle-passive participle nom. sg. masc., "being worn down, grieving." ἦτορ (ἦτορ): acc. sg. neut., "heart" (internal accusative with the participle). Telemachus sat among the suitors with his heart worn down by grief, thinking of his noble father.

lines.original: ὀσσόμενος πατέρʼ ἐσθλὸν ἐνὶ φρεσίν, εἴ ποθεν ἐλθὼν
lines.english: Looking for his noble father in his mind, if he should come from somewhere
lines.gloss: **ὀσσόμενος** (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc. from ὄσσομαι) "foreseeing, imagining"; **πατέρʼ ἐσθλόν** (acc. sg. masc., noun + adj.) "noble father"; **ἐνὶ φρεσίν** (prep. + dat. pl.) "in his mind/heart"; **ἐλθών** (aor. act. participle, nom. sg. masc. from ἔρχομαι) "having come, coming." Telemachus sits imagining in his mind his noble father, whether coming from somewhere he might scatter the suitors throughout the halls.

lines.original: μνηστήρων τῶν μὲν σκέδασιν κατὰ δώματα θείη,
lines.english: he might make a scattering of the suitors throughout the halls
lines.gloss: **μνηστήρων** (gen. pl. of μνηστήρ): "of the suitors" - genitive of separation depending on σκέδασιν. **σκέδασιν** (acc. sg. of σκέδασις): "scattering, dispersal" - direct object of θείη. **κατὰ δώματα**: "throughout the halls" - prepositional phrase with distributive sense. **θείη** (3rd sg. aor. opt. act. of τίθημι): "he might make/put" - potential optative expressing Telemachus's wish. Telemachus hopes his father might return and scatter the suitors dispersing them from the halls.

lines.original: τιμὴν δʼ αὐτὸς ἔχοι καὶ δώμασιν οἷσιν ἀνάσσοι.
lines.english: He himself would have honor and rule in his own house.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for:** τιμὴν δʼ αὐτὸς ἔχοι καὶ δώμασιν οἷσιν ἀνάσσοι.

**τιμήν** (acc. sg. fem., "honor/prerogative") – direct object of ἔχοι; **ἔχοι** (3rd sg. pres. opt. act., ἔχω, "might have/hold") – optative expressing a wish; **δώμασιν** (dat. pl. neut., δῶμα, "halls/house") – dative of place or sphere; **ἀνάσσοι** (3rd sg. pres. opt. act., ἀνάσσω, "might rule/be lord over") – parallel optative of wish. Telemachus wishes he himself might retain his honor

lines.original: τὰ φρονέων, μνηστῆρσι μεθήμενος, εἴσιδʼ Ἀθήνην.
lines.english: Thinking these thoughts, mingling with the suitors, he saw Athena.
lines.gloss:
**τὰ φρονέων, μνηστῆρσι μεθήμενος, εἴσιδʼ Ἀθήνην.**

φρονέων (pres. act. participle, nom. sg. masc. of φρονέω): "pondering, thinking [these things]"; μεθήμενος (aor. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc. of μεθίημι): "mingling with, going among"; μνηστῆρσι (dat. pl. of μνηστήρ): "the suitors"; εἴσιδε (3rd sg. aor. of εἶδον): "he saw"; Ἀθήνην (acc. sg.): "Athena." Telemachus, pondering these matters and moving among the suitors, caught sight of Athena.

lines.original: βῆ δʼ ἰθὺς προθύροιο, νεμεσσήθη δʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ
lines.english: He went straight to the doorway and was indignant in his heart.
lines.gloss: **βῆ** (3rd sg. aor. ind. of βαίνω) "he went"; **ἰθύς** (adv.) "straight toward" + gen. **προθύροιο** (gen. sg. of πρόθυρον) "the forecourt/doorway"; **νεμεσσήθη** (3rd sg. aor. ind. of νεμεσσάομαι) "he felt indignation"; **θυμῷ** (dat. sg. of θυμός) "in his heart/spirit." Telemachus went straight toward the doorway and felt indignation in his heart (at seeing the guest left standing outside).

lines.original: ξεῖνον δηθὰ θύρῃσιν ἐφεστάμεν· ἐγγύθι δὲ στὰς
lines.english: that a stranger should stand waiting so long at the doors, and stepping near
lines.gloss:
**ξεῖνον** (acc. sg. masc. of ξεῖνος): "guest/stranger," direct object of the infinitive ἐφεστάμεν. **δηθὰ** (adverb): "for a long time," modifying the infinitive. **θύρῃσιν** (dat. pl. of θύρη): "at the doors," locative dative. **ἐφεστάμεν** (perf. inf. of ἐφίστημι): "to have stood," explaining the cause of his indignation. **ἐγγύθι** (adverb): "near," with **στὰς** (aor. part. of ἵστημι), "standing near."

The line expresses Telemachus's self-reproach for keeping the guest/stranger standing at the doors for so long; he now stands

lines.original: χεῖρʼ ἕλε δεξιτερὴν καὶ ἐδέξατο χάλκεον ἔγχος,
lines.english: He took her right hand and received the bronze spear from her.
lines.gloss: **χεῖρʼ** (χεῖρα, acc. sg. fem. of χείρ): "hand" (direct object of ἕλε). **ἕλε** (3rd sg. aor. act. ind. of αἱρέω): "took, grasped." **δεξιτερὴν** (acc. sg. fem. of δεξιτερός): "right" (modifying χεῖρα). **ἐδέξατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. ind. of δέχομαι): "received, took." **χάλκεον ἔγχος** (acc. sg. neut.): "bronze spear" (direct object of ἐδέξατο). He took his right hand and received the bronze spear.

lines.original: καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
lines.english: And addressing him he spoke winged words.
lines.gloss: **φωνήσας** (nom. sg. masc. aor. act. participle of φωνέω): "addressing [him]"; **ἔπεα** (acc. pl. neut. of ἔπος): "words"; **πτερόεντα** (acc. pl. neut. of πτερόεις): "winged"; **προσηύδα** (3rd sg. impf. act. of προσαυδάω): "he/she spoke to [him]." The line describes someone addressing another with "winged words," a formulaic expression for swift or apt speech.

lines.original: ὣς εἰπὼν ἡγεῖθʼ, ἡ δʼ ἕσπετο Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη.
lines.english: So speaking he led the way, and Pallas Athena followed him.
lines.gloss: **ὣς** (adverb): "thus, in this way"—refers back to Odysseus's preceding speech. **εἰπών** (aorist active participle, nom. sg. masc. of *εἶπον*): "having spoken." **ἡγεῖθʼ** (imperfect middle, 3rd sg. of *ἡγέομαι*): "he led (the way)," with Odysseus as subject. **ἕσπετο** (imperfect middle, 3rd sg. of *ἕπομαι*): "she followed." **Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg.): "Pallas Athena," the goddess following Odysseus. The line depicts Odysseus leading the way after speaking, with Athena following behind him.

lines.original: οἱ δʼ ὅτε δή ῥʼ ἔντοσθεν ἔσαν δόμου ὑψηλοῖο,
lines.english: When they were inside the lofty house
lines.gloss:
**οἱ δʼ ὅτε δή ῥʼ ἔντοσθεν ἔσαν δόμου ὑψηλοῖο**

*ὅτε* (conj.): "when," introducing temporal clause. *ἔντοσθεν* (adv.): "inside, within." *ἔσαν* (3rd pl. impf. εἰμί): "they were." *δόμου* (gen. sg. δόμος): "of the house," genitive of place within which. *ὑψηλοῖο* (gen. sg. ὑψηλός): "lofty, high-roofed," epic genitive form modifying *δόμου*. They (Telemachus and Athena-Mentes) had now entered inside the lofty hall

lines.original: ἔγχος μέν ῥʼ ἔστησε φέρων πρὸς κίονα μακρὴν
lines.english: He set the spear he was carrying against a tall pillar.
lines.gloss:
**ἔγχος μέν ῥʼ ἔστησε φέρων πρὸς κίονα μακρήν**

**ἔγχος** (neut. acc. sg., "spear") is the object; **ἔστησε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἵστημι, "he set/stood") is the main verb; **φέρων** (pres. act. masc. nom. sg. participle of φέρω, "carrying/bringing") modifies the subject; **κίονα** (fem. acc. sg., "pillar/column") with **πρὸς** ("against") indicates the location. The line describes someone setting his spear against a tall pillar while carrying it inside.

lines.original: δουροδόκης ἔντοσθεν ἐυξόου, ἔνθα περ ἄλλα
lines.english: in the spear-stand inside the polished hall, where many other spears stood
lines.gloss:
**δουροδόκης** (gen. sg., "of the spear-stand"): from δουροδόκη, a compound of δόρυ ("spear") and δέχομαι ("receive"), denoting a rack or holder for spears. **ἔντοσθεν** (adv., "within, inside"): indicates position inside something. **ἐυξόου** (gen. sg., "well-polished"): adjective modifying δουροδόκης, from εὐ- ("well") + ξέω ("polish, smooth"). **ἄλλα** (nom./acc. pl. neut., "the others"): refers to the other spears already standing there.

The line describes the spear being placed within a well-polished spear-rack, where the other spears stood.

lines.original: ἔγχεʼ Ὀδυσσῆος ταλασίφρονος ἵστατο πολλά,
lines.english: where many spears of steadfast-hearted Odysseus stood.
lines.gloss: **ἔγχεʼ** (ἔγχεα, nom./acc. neut. pl. of ἔγχος): "spears"; **Ὀδυσσῆος** (gen. sg. of Ὀδυσσεύς): "of Odysseus," possessive genitive; **ταλασίφρονος** (gen. sg. masc. of ταλασίφρων): "steadfast-hearted, enduring," epithet modifying Odysseus; **ἵστατο** (3rd sg. pluperfect mid./pass. of ἵστημι): "stood, were positioned"; **πολλά** (nom./acc. neut. pl. of πολύς): "many." The line describes how many spears of steadfast Odysseus stood in the spear-rack.

lines.original: αὐτὴν δʼ ἐς θρόνον εἷσεν ἄγων, ὑπὸ λῖτα πετάσσας,
lines.english: He led her to a throne and seated her, spreading a linen cloth beneath.
lines.gloss:
**αὐτήν** (pronoun, fem. acc. sg. of αὐτός): "her" (Penelope herself, intensive). **θρόνον** (noun, masc. acc. sg. of θρόνος): "chair, seat." **εἷσεν** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἵζω): "he seated." **ἄγων** (participle, masc. nom. sg. pres. act. of ἄγω): "leading, bringing." **λῖτα** (noun, neut. acc. pl. of λίτον): "smooth linen cloths, woven fabrics." **πετάσσας** (participle, masc. nom. sg. aor. act. of πετάννυμι): "spreading out, unfolding."

He seated her herself on a chair,

lines.original: καλὸν δαιδάλεον· ὑπὸ δὲ θρῆνυς ποσὶν ἦεν.
lines.english: a beautiful intricate throne, and a footstool was beneath her feet.
lines.gloss: **καλὸν** (adj. acc. sg. masc.) "beautiful," modifying κλισμὸν from the previous line; **δαιδάλεον** (adj. acc. sg. masc.) "skillfully wrought, elaborately decorated"; **θρῆνυς** (noun nom. sg. masc.) "footstool"; **ποσὶν** (noun dat. pl.) "for the feet"; **ἦεν** (impf. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) "was, there was." The verse completes the description of the elaborate chair and notes that a footstool was positioned beneath it for the feet.

lines.original: πὰρ δʼ αὐτὸς κλισμὸν θέτο ποικίλον, ἔκτοθεν ἄλλων
lines.english: She set a richly-wrought chair for him apart from the others.
lines.gloss:
**πὰρ δʼ αὐτὸς κλισμὸν θέτο ποικίλον, ἔκτοθεν ἄλλων**

**αὐτὸς** (intensive pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "himself" (i.e., Odysseus/the host personally). **κλισμὸν** (noun, accusative singular masculine): "chair, seat," direct object of θέτο. **θέτο** (verb, 3rd singular aorist middle indicative of τίθημι): "placed, set." **ποικίλον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine): "ornate, elaborately wrought," modifying κλισμὸν. **ἔκτοθεν** (adverb with genitive): "apart from, away from," with **ἄλλων** (gen

lines.original: μνηστήρων, μὴ ξεῖνος ἀνιηθεὶς ὀρυμαγδῷ
lines.english: away from the suitors, lest the stranger be distressed by their clamor
lines.gloss:
**μνηστήρων** (gen. pl., μνηστήρ): "of the suitors" - genitive of source/separation dependent on the previous line. **ξεῖνος** (nom. sg., ξεῖνος): "the guest/stranger" - subject, referring to Odysseus in disguise. **ἀνιηθεὶς** (aor. pass. ptc., ἀνιάω): "being distressed/grieved" - circumstantial participle modifying ξεῖνος. **ὀρυμαγδῷ** (dat. sg., ὀρυμαγδός): "by the uproar/tumult" - dative of cause expressing what would distress the guest.

The line expresses Telemachus' concern that the guest not be distressed by the suitors' riotous behavior at the feast.

lines.original: δείπνῳ ἁδήσειεν, ὑπερφιάλοισι μετελθών,
lines.english: lest the stranger, coming among the arrogant suitors, take no pleasure in the feast.
lines.gloss:
**δείπνῳ** (noun, dative singular neuter of δεῖπνον): "at the feast" or "with the meal" – dative of time or manner.

**ἁδήσειεν** (verb, 3rd singular aorist optative active of ἁνδάνω): "might take pleasure" or "might enjoy" – potential/purpose optative expressing the hoped-for result.

**ὑπερφιάλοισι** (adjective, dative plural masculine/neuter of ὑπερφίαλος): "among the arrogant/insolent ones" – refers to the suitors; dative of association.

**μετελθών** (verb, aorist participle masculine nominative singular of μέτειμι): "having gone among" or "having mingled with" – circumstantial participle modifying the subject (the stranger/guest).

lines.original: ἠδʼ ἵνα μιν περὶ πατρὸς ἀποιχομένοιο ἔροιτο.
lines.english: and so that he might ask him about his absent father.
lines.gloss:
**ἠδέ** (conj.) "and" or "and also" — connects this purpose clause to the preceding thought.

**ἵνα** (conj.) "in order that, so that" — introduces a purpose clause with subjunctive **ἔροιτο**.

**περί** (prep. + gen.) "about, concerning" — governs **πατρός**, indicating the topic of inquiry.

**πατρός** (noun, gen. sg.) "father" — object of the preposition, referring to Odysseus.

**ἀποιχομένοιο** (participle, pres. mid./pass. gen. sg. from ἀποίχομαι) "having gone away, absent" — modifies **πατρός**, describing the father's departed state.

**ἔροιτο** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. mid. opt. from

lines.original: χέρνιβα δʼ ἀμφίπολος προχόῳ ἐπέχευε φέρουσα
lines.english: A maidservant poured water for their hands, bringing it from a pitcher.
lines.gloss: **χέρνιβα** (acc. neut. pl., χέρνιψ) "hand-washing water"; **ἀμφίπολος** (nom. fem. sg.) "handmaid, attendant"; **προχόῳ** (dat. fem. sg., προχόη) "pitcher, ewer" (instrumental dative); **ἐπέχευε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἐπιχέω) "poured over/upon"; **φέρουσα** (nom. fem. sg. pres. part., φέρω) "carrying, bearing." The handmaid poured hand-washing water from a pitcher she was carrying, a standard element of Homeric hospitality ritual.

lines.original: καλῇ χρυσείῃ, ὑπὲρ ἀργυρέοιο λέβητος,
lines.english: from a beautiful golden pitcher over a silver basin
lines.gloss: **καλῇ** (adj., dat. sg. fem.): beautiful, describing the golden pitcher; **χρυσείῃ** (adj., dat. sg. fem.): golden, modifying προχόῳ (pitcher) from the previous line; **ὑπέρ** (prep. + gen.): over, above; **ἀργυρέοιο** (adj., gen. sg. masc./neut.): silver, of silver; **λέβητος** (noun, gen. sg. masc.): basin, cauldron. The maidservant pours water from a beautiful golden pitcher over a silver basin for hand-washing.

lines.original: νίψασθαι· παρὰ δὲ ξεστὴν ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν.
lines.english: to wash, and she drew up beside them a polished table.
lines.gloss:
**νίψασθαι·** aorist middle infinitive of νίπτω, "to wash (oneself)," expressing purpose. **παρὰ δέ:** adverb with postpositive conjunction, "beside" or "near at hand." **ξεστήν:** feminine accusative singular adjective modifying τράπεζαν, "polished" or "smooth." **ἐτάνυσσε:** third singular aorist of τανύω, "she set out" or "she spread." **τράπεζαν:** feminine accusative singular noun, "table."

The line describes washing followed by setting out a polished table, typical hospitality actions in Homeric scenes.

lines.original: σῖτον δʼ αἰδοίη ταμίη παρέθηκε φέρουσα,
lines.english: The respected housekeeper brought and set out bread beside them.
lines.gloss: **σῖτον** (acc. sing. masc., "bread/food") δ(έ) (postpositive particle, "and/now") **αἰδοίη** (nom. sing. fem., "reverend/respected") **ταμίη** (nom. sing. fem., "housekeeper") **παρέθηκε** (3rd sing. aor. indic. act. of παρατίθημι, "set before/served") **φέρουσα** (nom. sing. fem. pres. part. of φέρω, "carrying/bringing"). The respected housekeeper served bread, bringing and setting it before them.

lines.original: εἴδατα πόλλʼ ἐπιθεῖσα, χαριζομένη παρεόντων·
lines.english: laying out many kinds of food, graciously giving from what was at hand
lines.gloss: **εἴδατα** (nom./acc. pl. neut. of εἶδαρ) "meats, food" serves as direct object of the participle. **πόλλʼ** (nom./acc. pl. neut. of πολύς) "many" modifies εἴδατα. **ἐπιθεῖσα** (aor. act. fem. nom. sg. participle of ἐπιτίθημι) "having placed upon, having set forth" describes the housekeeper's action. **χαριζομένη** (pres. mid. fem. nom. sg. participle of χαρίζομαι) "showing favor, pleasing" expresses manner. **παρεόντων** (gen. pl. pres. participle of πάρειμι) "of those present" functions as objective genitive with χαριζ

lines.original: δαιτρὸς δὲ κρειῶν πίνακας παρέθηκεν ἀείρας
lines.english: The carver set before them platters of meat he had lifted up.
lines.gloss: **δαιτρός** (noun, nominative singular): "carver," the official who distributes meat at feasts. **κρειῶν** (noun, genitive plural, from κρέας): "of meats." **πίνακας** (noun, accusative plural): "platters" or "serving boards." **παρέθηκεν** (verb, 3rd singular aorist active indicative, from παρατίθημι): "set beside" or "served." **ἀείρας** (participle, aorist active nominative singular, from ἀείρω): "having lifted up" or "raising." The carver served platters of meats, having lifted them up and placed them beside the guests.

lines.original: παντοίων, παρὰ δέ σφι τίθει χρύσεια κύπελλα·
lines.english: of all kinds, and set golden cups beside them.
lines.gloss:
**παντοίων** (gen. pl. adj. from παντοῖος): "of all kinds," modifying κρειῶν from the previous line, describing the various meats. **παρά** (prep. + dat.): "beside," indicating placement near them. **σφι** (dat. pl. pronoun, enclitic): "for them/to them," indirect object. **τίθει** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of τίθημι): "he placed/set down," main verb. **χρύσεια** (nom./acc. pl. neut. adj. from χρύσεος): "golden," modifying **κύπελλα** (nom./acc. pl. neut. noun): "cups/goblets," direct object.

The carver set out golden cups beside them (to hold meats) of all kinds.

lines.original: κῆρυξ δʼ αὐτοῖσιν θάμʼ ἐπῴχετο οἰνοχοεύων.
lines.english: A herald went back and forth among them pouring wine.
lines.gloss: **κῆρυξ** (nom. sg. masc., "herald") is the subject; **αὐτοῖσιν** (dat. pl. masc., "for them/to them") indicates the beneficiaries of the action; **θάμʼ** (adverb, crasis for θαμά, "frequently/often") modifies the verb; **ἐπῴχετο** (3rd sg. imperf. mid., "went about/moved among"); **οἰνοχοεύων** (pres. part. nom. sg. masc., "pouring wine"). The herald frequently went about among them serving wine to the suitors.

lines.original: ἐς δʼ ἦλθον μνηστῆρες ἀγήνορες. οἱ μὲν ἔπειτα
lines.english: The proud suitors entered, and then they
lines.gloss:
**ἐς δʼ ἦλθον μνηστῆρες ἀγήνορες. οἱ μὲν ἔπειτα**

Key words: **ἦλθον** (aorist, 3rd pl. of ἔρχομαι, "they came"); **μνηστῆρες** (nom. pl., "suitors"); **ἀγήνορες** (nom. pl. adj., "proud, arrogant"). The proud suitors arrived, and then (continuing in the next line) they sat down in order on benches and chairs.

lines.original: ἑξείης ἕζοντο κατὰ κλισμούς τε θρόνους τε,
lines.english: They sat down in order on the chairs and thrones.
lines.gloss:
**ἑξείης** (adverb): "in a row," "in order," describing how the suitors took their seats in succession.

**ἕζοντο** (verb, 3rd pl. imperfect middle, from ἕζομαι): "they sat down," the suitors assuming their positions.

**κλισμούς** (noun, acc. pl. masculine, κλισμός): "chairs," specifically reclining chairs or couches.

**θρόνους** (noun, acc. pl. masculine, θρόνος): "thrones," high-backed ornate seats of honor.

The suitors seated themselves in orderly fashion upon the various chairs and thrones in Odysseus's hall.

lines.original: τοῖσι δὲ κήρυκες μὲν ὕδωρ ἐπὶ χεῖρας ἔχευαν,
lines.english: Heralds poured water over their hands for washing.
lines.gloss: **κήρυκες** (nom. pl. masc., "heralds") serve as **subject**; **ὕδωρ** (acc. sing. neut., "water") is the **direct object**; **ἐπὶ χεῖρας** (prep. + acc. pl. fem., "upon [their] hands") indicates where the water is poured; **ἔχευαν** (3rd pl. impf. act., "they poured") is the main verb. The heralds pour water over the hands of the assembled guests as part of the ritual preparation for the meal.

lines.original: σῖτον δὲ δμῳαὶ παρενήνεον ἐν κανέοισιν,
lines.english: Serving maids heaped up bread in baskets beside them.
lines.gloss: **σῖτον** (acc. sing. masc., "grain/bread") - object of the verb, the food being distributed. **δμῳαί** (nom. pl. fem., "female servants/handmaids") - subject performing the action. **παρενήνεον** (3rd pl. impf. act., παρα-νέω) - "heaped up beside" or "piled high," describing the serving action. **κανέοισιν** (dat. pl. neut., "baskets") - containers in which the bread is presented. The female servants distribute heaps of bread in baskets as part of the feast preparation.

lines.original: κοῦροι δὲ κρητῆρας ἐπεστέψαντο ποτοῖο.
lines.english: The young men filled the mixing bowls to the brim with drink.
lines.gloss: **κοῦροι** (nom. pl. masc., "young men/servants") **δὲ** (particle, "and/but") **κρητῆρας** (acc. pl. masc., "mixing-bowls") **ἐπεστέψαντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. ind. of ἐπιστέφω, "they crowned/filled to the brim") **ποτοῖο** (gen. sg. neut., "of drink/wine"). The young men filled the mixing-bowls with wine to the brim, a typical symposiastic preparation scene where wine is mixed with water in kraters before distribution.

lines.original: οἱ δʼ ἐπʼ ὀνείαθʼ ἑτοῖμα προκείμενα χεῖρας ἴαλλον.
lines.english: They stretched forth their hands to the good things lying ready before them.
lines.gloss:
**οἱ δ' ἐπ' ὀνείαθ' ἑτοῖμα προκείμενα χεῖρας ἴαλλον.**

**ὀνείαθ'** (ὀνείατα, neut. pl. acc.): "delicacies," "good things (to eat)," object of ἴαλλον. **ἑτοῖμα** (adj. neut. pl. acc.): "ready," "prepared," modifying ὀνείατα. **προκείμενα** (pres. mid. participle, neut. pl. acc.): "lying before (them)," further describing the food. **χεῖρας** (fem. pl. acc.): "hands," direct object. **ἴαλλον** (impf. act. 3rd

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο
lines.english: But when they had satisfied their desire for food and drink
lines.gloss: **ἐπεί** (conj.) "when, after" introduces temporal clause. **πόσιος** (gen. sg. of πόσις) "of drink" and **ἐδητύος** (gen. sg. of ἐδητύς) "of food" are genitives of separation dependent on **ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. of ἵημι) "they had their fill of, satisfied their desire for." This formulaic line marks the transition from feasting to subsequent action.

lines.original: μνηστῆρες, τοῖσιν μὲν ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ἄλλα μεμήλει,
lines.english: The suitors, for them other things were on their minds
lines.gloss: **μνηστῆρες** (nom. pl. masc., "suitors") **τοῖσιν** (dat. pl. masc., "for them/these") **φρεσὶν** (dat. pl. fem., "in minds/hearts," from φρήν) **ἄλλα** (nom./acc. pl. neut., "other things") **μεμήλει** (3rd sg. pluperfect, "was a care/concern," from μέλω). The suitors had other concerns in their minds—the perfect tense indicates their attention was fixed elsewhere, contrasting with the normal festive pursuits of song and dance mentioned in the surrounding context.

lines.original: μολπή τʼ ὀρχηστύς τε· τὰ γάρ τʼ ἀναθήματα δαιτός·
lines.english: Song and dance, for these are the adornments of a feast.
lines.gloss:
**μολπή τʼ ὀρχηστύς τε· τὰ γάρ τʼ ἀναθήματα δαιτός·**

Key words: **μολπή** (nom. sing. fem., "song, dance with song"), **ὀρχηστύς** (nom. sing. fem., "dancing"), **ἀναθήματα** (nom. pl. neut., "accompaniments, adornments"), **δαιτός** (gen. sing. fem., "of the feast"). The line explains that song and dance are the accompaniments/embellishments of a feast, accounting for the suitors' different concerns mentioned in the previous line.

lines.original: κῆρυξ δʼ ἐν χερσὶν κίθαριν περικαλλέα θῆκεν
lines.english: The herald placed a very beautiful lyre in his hands.
lines.gloss: **κῆρυξ** (nom. sg. masc., "herald") is the subject; **ἐν χερσίν** (dat. pl. fem., "in/into the hands") shows location; **κίθαριν περικαλλέα** (acc. sg. fem., "very beautiful lyre," with **περικαλλέα** < περικαλλής) is the object; **θῆκεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of τίθημι, "placed/put"). The herald placed the beautiful lyre into the hands (of Phemius, as the next line reveals).

lines.original: Φημίῳ, ὅς ῥʼ ἤειδε παρὰ μνηστῆρσιν ἀνάγκῃ.
lines.english: for Phemius, who sang among the suitors under compulsion.
lines.gloss:
**Φημίῳ** (dat. sg. masc., proper name): to Phemius, the bard. **ὅς** (nom. sg. masc., relative pronoun): who. **ἤειδε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἀείδω): was singing, sang. **μνηστῆρσιν** (dat. pl. masc., μνηστήρ): among/for the suitors. **ἀνάγκῃ** (dat. sg. fem., ἀνάγκη): under compulsion, by necessity.

The herald placed the beautiful lyre in the hands of Phemius, who sang among the suitors under compulsion.

lines.original: ἦ τοι ὁ φορμίζων ἀνεβάλλετο καλὸν ἀείδειν.
lines.english: He struck up his lyre and began to sing beautifully.
lines.gloss:
**ἦ τοι** (particle): "and so," "indeed then" (transitional phrase marking continuation of narrative)
**φορμίζων** (present participle, nominative singular masculine, from φορμίζω): "playing the lyre," "accompanying on the phorminx"
**ἀνεβάλλετο** (imperfect middle, 3rd singular, from ἀναβάλλω): "he began," "struck up" (inceptive sense with middle voice)
**καλὸν ἀείδειν** (adjective + present infinitive): "to sing beautifully" (adverbial accusative with complementary infinitive)

The bard Phemius, accompanying himself on the lyre, began to sing beautifully for the suitors.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ Τηλέμαχος προσέφη γλαυκῶπιν Ἀθήνην,
lines.english: But Telemachos spoke to glaukopis Athena
lines.gloss:
**Τηλέμαχος** (nom. sg. masc., proper noun): Telemachus, subject of the verb.
**προσέφη** (3rd sg. aor. indic. mid., προσ-φημί): "addressed," "spoke to."
**γλαυκῶπιν** (acc. sg. fem., γλαυκῶπις): "bright-eyed," "grey-eyed," epithet modifying Athena.
**Ἀθήνην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Athena, direct object.

Telemachus addresses the disguised Athena, speaking to her apart from the other suitors.

lines.original: ἄγχι σχὼν κεφαλήν, ἵνα μὴ πευθοίαθʼ οἱ ἄλλοι·
lines.english: holding his head close so that the others might not hear
lines.gloss:
**ἄγχι σχὼν κεφαλήν, ἵνα μὴ πευθοίαθʼ οἱ ἄλλοι·**

**ἄγχι** (adverb): "near, close by" — **σχών** (aorist active participle of ἔχω, nom. masc. sing.): "holding" — **κεφαλήν** (acc. sing.): "head" — **πευθοίαθʼ** (aorist middle optative, 3rd pl. of πυνθάνομαι): "might learn, perceive" — **ἄλλοι** (nom. masc. pl.): "the others." Telemachus holds his head close (to Athena) so that the others might not overhear their conversation.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖτε προσέειπε θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: The goddess, grey-eyed Athena, then spoke to him in reply.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 

- **προσέειπε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of προσεῖπον): "addressed," "spoke to"
- **θεά** (nom. sg. fem.): "goddess," subject of the verb
- **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. adj.): "grey-eyed," "bright-eyed," epithet modifying Athena
- **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg. fem.): "Athena," the goddess in apposition to θεά

The grey-eyed goddess Athena then addressed him in response (τὸν δʼ αὖτε), with the particle αὖτε marking the continuation of dialogue.

lines.original: τὴν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: And then wise Telemachos answered her in turn.
lines.gloss: **Τηλέμαχος** (nom. sg. masc., proper noun) "Telemachus," subject; **πεπνυμένος** (perf. part. nom. sg. masc., πέπνυμαι) "wise, prudent," modifying Telemachus; **ἀντίον** (adv.) "in response, in turn"; **ηὔδα** (3rd sg. aor. indic., αὐδάω) "spoke, addressed." Telemachus, characterized as wise/prudent, responds in turn to Athena (τήν = her, acc. sg. fem.).

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖτε προσέειπε θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: Then the goddess, grey-eyed Athena, addressed him in turn.
lines.gloss: **προσέειπε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of προσεῖπον) "addressed"; **θεά** (nom. sg. fem. noun) "goddess"; **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. epithet) "grey-eyed, bright-eyed"; **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg. proper noun) "Athena." The goddess Athena, identified by her traditional Homeric epithet "grey-eyed," spoke to him in response.

lines.original: τὴν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: Then thoughtful Telemachos spoke to her in reply.
lines.gloss: **Τηλέμαχος** (nominative singular, proper noun): Telemachus, subject. **πεπνυμένος** (perfect passive participle, nominative singular masculine from *πέπνυμαι*): "prudent," "wise," "sensible," modifying Telemachus. **ἀντίον** (adverb): "in reply," "in response." **ηὔδα** (3rd singular imperfect active indicative of *αὐδάω*): "spoke," "addressed." Telemachus, being prudent/wise, speaks in response to her (Athena).

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἐπαλαστήσασα προσηύδα Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: Pallas Athena, drawing near to him, addressed him.
lines.gloss:
**ἐπαλαστήσασα** (aorist participle, nominative feminine singular of ἐπαλαστέω): "approaching" or "drawing near to him." **προσηύδα** (imperfect, 3rd singular of προσαυδάω): "addressed" or "spoke to." **Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη** (nominative singular): "Pallas Athena," the goddess. 

Pallas Athena, drawing near to him (Telemachus), addressed him.

lines.original: τὴν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: And Telemachus, being thoughtful, spoke to her in turn.
lines.gloss:
**τὴν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·**

**τὴν** (pronoun, accusative singular feminine) = "her"; **αὖ** (particle) = "in turn, again"; **Τηλέμαχος** (proper noun, nominative singular) = "Telemachus"; **πεπνυμένος** (perfect middle/passive participle, nominative singular masculine from πέπνυμαι) = "prudent, wise"; **ἀντίον** (adverb) = "in reply, face-to-face"; **ηὔδα** (3rd singular imperfect active indicative of αὐδάω) = "addressed, spoke." Telemachus, characterized as thoughtful/prudent, responds directly to her (

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἠμείβετʼ ἔπειτα θεά, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: Then the goddess, bright-eyed Athena, answered him in turn.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἠμείβετο (ἀμείβω, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic., "answered"); θεά (nom. sg., "goddess"); γλαυκῶπις (nom. sg. fem. epithet, "grey-eyed"); Ἀθήνη (nom. sg., "Athena"). 

The goddess grey-eyed Athena then answered him (Telemachus), with the formulaic epithet emphasizing her divine identity and characteristic appearance.

lines.original: ἡ μὲν ἄρʼ ὣς εἰποῦσʼ ἀπέβη γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη,
lines.english: Having spoken thus, the gleaming-eyed Athena departed.
lines.gloss:
**ἡ μὲν ἄρʼ ὣς εἰποῦσʼ ἀπέβη γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·**

**εἰποῦσʼ** (εἰποῦσα): aorist active participle, nominative feminine singular of εἶπον, "having spoken." **ἀπέβη**: third singular aorist indicative of ἀποβαίνω, "she went away, departed." **γλαυκῶπις**: nominative feminine singular epithet, "grey-eyed" (modifying Athena). The line describes Athena's departure after speaking, with the particles μέν...ἄρʼ and ὣς framing her action.

lines.original: ὄρνις δʼ ὣς ἀνόπαια διέπτατο· τῷ δʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ
lines.english: She flew through the upper air like a bird, and in his heart
lines.gloss:
**ὄρνις** (nom. sg. m.) "bird" - subject describing Athena's departure. **ἀνόπαια** (adv.) "upward through the smoke-hole" - indicates her manner of flight through the roof opening. **διέπτατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of διαπέτομαι) "she flew through/away" - main verb of Athena's aerial departure. **θυμῷ** (dat. sg. m.) "in his heart/spirit" - locative dative indicating where Telemachus experiences the following emotions (completed in next line).

Athena departs like a bird flying upward through the roof's smoke-hole, while in Telemachus's heart (the goddess's action produces effects described in the subsequent line).

lines.original: θῆκε μένος καὶ θάρσος, ὑπέμνησέν τέ ἑ πατρὸς
lines.english: She put courage and boldness in his heart and made him think of his father.
lines.gloss: **θῆκε** (aorist active indicative 3rd sg. of τίθημι) "placed, put" – the goddess Athena instilled in him; **μένος** (noun, acc. sg. neut.) "strength, might"; **θάρσος** (noun, acc. sg. neut.) "courage, boldness"; **ὑπέμνησέν** (aorist active indicative 3rd sg. of ὑπομιμνῄσκω) "reminded"; **πατρός** (noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of [his] father." Athena placed strength and courage in Telemachus and reminded him of his father Odysseus.

lines.original: μᾶλλον ἔτʼ ἢ τὸ πάροιθεν. ὁ δὲ φρεσὶν ᾗσι νοήσας
lines.english: even more than before, and he perceiving it in his mind
lines.gloss:
**μᾶλλον** (adverb): "more," comparative degree modifying the understood courage/spirit from the previous line. **πάροιθεν** (adverb): "before, formerly," temporal reference to an earlier time. **φρεσὶν** (noun): dative plural of φρήν, "mind, heart," instrumental dative indicating the faculty with which he perceives. **ᾗσι** (pronoun): dative plural feminine of ὅς (possessive), "his own," agreeing with φρεσίν. **νοήσας** (verb): aorist active participle of νοέω, nominative singular masculine, "having perceived/understood."

The line intensifies Telemachus' courage beyond what it was before, while the hero (likely Odysseus) perceives something in his own mind/heart.

lines.original: θάμβησεν κατὰ θυμόν· ὀίσατο γὰρ θεὸν εἶναι.
lines.english: He was amazed in his heart, for he thought her to be a god.
lines.gloss: **θάμβησεν** (θαμβέω, 3rd sg. aor. act. ind.) "he was amazed/astonished"; **κατὰ θυμόν** (prep. + acc.) "in his heart/spirit"; **ὀίσατο** (οἴομαι, 3rd sg. aor. mid. ind.) "he thought/supposed"; **θεὸν εἶναι** (acc. + pres. inf.) "to be a god." Telemachus was astonished in his heart, for he thought (Athena-Mentes) to be a god.

lines.original: αὐτίκα δὲ μνηστῆρας ἐπῴχετο ἰσόθεος φώς.
lines.english: At once the godlike man went toward the suitors.
lines.gloss:
**αὐτίκα** (adverb): "immediately, at once" — temporal marker indicating swift transition.

**μνηστῆρας** (noun, acc. pl. masculine): "suitors" — the men courting Penelope, object of the verb.

**ἐπῴχετο** (verb, 3rd sg. imperfect middle): "went among, approached" — from ἐπέρχομαι, depicting the hero's movement toward the suitors.

**ἰσόθεος** (adjective, nom. sg. masculine): "godlike, equal to the gods" — epic epithet modifying φώς.

**φώς** (noun, nom. sg. masculine): "man, hero" — subject, referring to Odysseus in his transformed appearance.

lines.original: τοῖσι δʼ ἀοιδὸς ἄειδε περικλυτός, οἱ δὲ σιωπῇ
lines.english: Among them a famous bard was singing, and they in silence
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 
- **τοῖσι** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural): "for them/to them" (the suitors)
- **ἀοιδὸς** (noun, nominative singular): "the singer/bard" 
- **ἄειδε** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect active): "was singing"
- **περικλυτός** (adjective, nominative singular): "very famous, renowned"
- **σιωπῇ** (noun, dative singular): "in silence"

The famous bard was singing for the suitors, who sat listening in silence.

lines.original: ἥατʼ ἀκούοντες· ὁ δʼ Ἀχαιῶν νόστον ἄειδε
lines.english: They sat listening in silence, and he sang of the Achaeans' homecoming.
lines.gloss:
**ἥατʼ ἀκούοντες· ὁ δʼ Ἀχαιῶν νόστον ἄειδε**

**ἥατο** (ἧμαι): 3rd pl. pluperfect middle, "they sat" or "were seated." **ἀκούοντες**: present participle nominative plural masculine of ἀκούω, "listening." **Ἀχαιῶν**: genitive plural, "of the Achaeans." **νόστον**: accusative singular of νόστος, "return, homecoming." **ἄειδε**: 3rd sg. imperfect active of ἀείδω, "he sang." The audience sat listening while the bard sang of the Achaeans' fateful return from Troy.

lines.original: λυγρόν, ὃν ἐκ Τροίης ἐπετείλατο Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη.
lines.english: the woeful return from Troy which Pallas Athena had laid upon the Achaeans
lines.gloss: **λυγρόν** (adj., acc. sing. masc.) "mournful, grievous" — modifies νόστον from the previous line, describing the sorrowful nature of the Achaeans' return. **ἐκ Τροίης** (prep. + gen.) "from Troy" — indicates origin of the homecoming journey. **ἐπετείλατο** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. mid. indic. from ἐπιτέλλω) "brought about, accomplished" — Pallas Athena caused or decreed this woeful return. **Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη** (proper noun, nom.) "Pallas Athena" — the goddess as the divine agent responsible for the disastrous homecoming.

lines.original: τοῦ δʼ ὑπερωιόθεν φρεσὶ σύνθετο θέσπιν ἀοιδὴν
lines.english: She heard from the upper chamber in her heart the divine song of the bard.
lines.gloss:
**τοῦ** (genitive singular masculine, demonstrative pronoun) "of him/his" – refers to the singer. **ὑπερωιόθεν** (adverb) "from the upper chamber" – indicates Penelope's location above. **φρεσὶ** (dative plural, φρήν) "in her mind/heart" – seat of thought and perception. **σύνθετο** (3rd singular aorist middle, συντίθημι) "perceived, understood, became aware of." **θέσπιν** (accusative singular feminine, θέσπις) "divine, wondrous" – modifies song. **ἀοιδήν** (accusative singular, ἀοιδή) "song."

Penelope, from her upper chamber, perceived in her mind the divine song of the bard (likely Phemius singing of the Achaeans

lines.original: κούρη Ἰκαρίοιο, περίφρων Πηνελόπεια·
lines.english: the daughter of Ikarios, wise Penelope
lines.gloss:
**κούρη Ἰκαρίοιο, περίφρων Πηνελόπεια·**

**κούρη** (nom. sg. fem., "daughter") of **Ἰκαρίοιο** (gen. sg. masc., "of Icarius"), **περίφρων** (nom. sg. fem. adj., "very wise, prudent") **Πηνελόπεια** (nom. sg. fem., "Penelope"). The daughter of Icarius, wise Penelope, is identified in apposition to the subject who has been listening from above and now descends.

lines.original: κλίμακα δʼ ὑψηλὴν κατεβήσετο οἷο δόμοιο,
lines.english: She descended the high stairway of her house.
lines.gloss: **κλίμακα** (acc. sg. fem., "staircase") serves as direct object of **κατεβήσετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. of καταβαίνω, "she descended"). **ὑψηλήν** (acc. sg. fem., "lofty, high") modifies κλίμακα. **οἷο δόμοιο** (gen. sg. masc., "of her house") expresses source or location. Penelope descends the high staircase of her house.

lines.original: οὐκ οἴη, ἅμα τῇ γε καὶ ἀμφίπολοι δύʼ ἕποντο.
lines.english: Not alone, for two handmaids followed along with her.
lines.gloss:
**οὐκ οἴη, ἅμα τῇ γε καὶ ἀμφίπολοι δύʼ ἕποντο.**

**οἴη** (nom. fem. sing. of οἶος, "alone"): negated by οὐκ, "not alone." **ἅμα** (adv., "together with") with **τῇ** (dat. sing. fem. of article, "her"). **ἀμφίπολοι** (nom. pl. fem., "handmaidens, attendants"). **δύο** (elided as δύʼ, "two"). **ἕποντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid. of ἕπομαι, "were following"). Penelope descends not alone but accompanied by two handmaidens following with her.

lines.original: ἡ δʼ ὅτε δὴ μνηστῆρας ἀφίκετο δῖα γυναικῶν,
lines.english: And when she, most noble of women, came to the suitors
lines.gloss: **ἀφίκετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ἀφικνέομαι) "arrived at, reached"; **μνηστῆρας** (acc. pl. masc. of μνηστήρ) "suitors"; **δῖα γυναικῶν** (nom. sg. fem. δῖα + gen. pl. γυναικῶν) "divine/noble among women." Penelope, identified by the formulaic epithet "divine among women," arrives at the location of the suitors, continuing her movement from the previous lines.

lines.original: στῆ ῥα παρὰ σταθμὸν τέγεος πύκα ποιητοῖο,
lines.english: She stood by the doorpost of the strongly-built hall.
lines.gloss: **στῆ** (3rd sing. aor. act. indic. of ἵστημι) "she stood"; **σταθμόν** (acc. sing. masc. of σταθμός) "doorpost, pillar"; **τέγεος** (gen. sing. neut. of τέγος) "of the hall, roof"; **πύκα** (adv.) "firmly, closely"; **ποιητοῖο** (gen. sing. masc./neut. of ποιητός) "well-made, constructed." Penelope takes her position beside the doorpost of the well-built hall, preparing to address the suitors from this architecturally strategic location.

lines.original: ἄντα παρειάων σχομένη λιπαρὰ κρήδεμνα·
lines.english: holding the shining veil before her cheeks
lines.gloss:
**ἄντα** (adv.): "opposite, before" – modifying the position relative to the face. **παρειάων** (gen. pl., fem.): "of the cheeks" – genitive of παρειά, limiting the position described. **σχομένη** (aor. mid. ptc., nom. sg. fem.): "holding" – from ἔχω, describing the subject's action. **λιπαρὰ** (acc. pl. neut.): "shining, glistening" – epithet modifying κρήδεμνα. **κρήδεμνα** (acc. pl. neut.): "headdress, veil" – object of σχομένη, the cloth held before the face.

The line describes a woman (likely Penelope) holding her shining veil before her cheeks in a gesture of modesty.

lines.original: ἀμφίπολος δʼ ἄρα οἱ κεδνὴ ἑκάτερθε παρέστη.
lines.english: A devoted handmaid stood beside her on either side.
lines.gloss: **ἀμφίπολος** (nom. sing. fem., "handmaid"), **κεδνή** (nom. sing. fem. adj., "trusty, faithful"), **ἑκάτερθε** (adv., "on each side"), **παρέστη** (3rd sing. aor., παρίστημι, "stood beside"). A trusty handmaid stood on each side of her (Penelope), providing support as she weeps and prepares to address the bard.

lines.original: δακρύσασα δʼ ἔπειτα προσηύδα θεῖον ἀοιδόν·
lines.english: Then weeping she addressed the godlike singer.
lines.gloss:
**δακρύσασα** (aorist participle, feminine nominative singular of δακρύω): "having wept" or "weeping." **ἔπειτα** (adverb): "then" or "thereupon." **προσηύδα** (3rd singular imperfect of προσαυδάω): "she addressed" or "spoke to." **θεῖον** (adjective, masculine accusative singular of θεῖος): "divine" or "godlike." **ἀοιδόν** (noun, masculine accusative singular of ἀοιδός): "singer" or "bard." 

Then weeping, she addressed the divine bard.

lines.original: τὴν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: Then wise Telemachos addressed her in turn.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τὴν (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular feminine) = "her" (i.e., Penelope); πεπνυμένος (perfect middle/passive participle, nominative singular masculine, from πέπνυμαι) = "prudent, sensible"; ἀντίον (adverb) = "in reply, in response"; ηὔδα (3rd singular aorist indicative active, from αὐδάω) = "addressed, spoke to."

Telemachus, characterized as "prudent/sensible," responds directly to Penelope, addressing her in reply to her previous speech to the bard.

lines.original: ἡ μὲν θαμβήσασα πάλιν οἶκόνδε βεβήκει·
lines.english: She went back home in amazement, for she took his thoughtful words to heart.
lines.gloss:
**ἡ μὲν θαμβήσασα πάλιν οἶκόνδε βεβήκει·**

θαμβήσασα (aorist participle, nominative feminine singular, from θαμβέω): "having marveled/been amazed"; βεβήκει (pluperfect active, 3rd singular, from βαίνω): "had gone"; οἶκόνδε (adverb): "homeward, to her house." She (Eurycleia or another woman) departed back home, amazed at Telemachus's wise words.

lines.original: παιδὸς γὰρ μῦθον πεπνυμένον ἔνθετο θυμῷ.
lines.english: For she took to heart the thoughtful words of her son.
lines.gloss:
**παιδός** (gen. sg. m. of παῖς): "of her son," governed by μῦθον. **μῦθον** (acc. sg. m. of μῦθος): "the word/speech," direct object of ἔνθετο. **πεπνυμένον** (acc. sg. m. perf. part. of *πέπνυμαι*): "prudent/wise," modifying μῦθον. **ἔνθετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. of τίθημι): "she placed/stored." **θυμῷ** (dat. sg. m. of θυμός): "in her heart," locative dative.

The line means "for she stored in her heart the wise words of her son."

lines.original: ἐς δʼ ὑπερῷʼ ἀναβᾶσα σὺν ἀμφιπόλοισι γυναιξὶ
lines.english: Going up to the upper chamber with her attendant women
lines.gloss:
**ἐς δʼ ὑπερῷʼ ἀναβᾶσα σὺν ἀμφιπόλοισι γυναιξὶ**

Key words: **ὑπερῷον** (n. acc. sg.) "upper chamber"; **ἀναβᾶσα** (aor. ptc. fem. nom. sg. from ἀναβαίνω) "having gone up"; **ἀμφιπόλοισι** (f. dat. pl.) "with attendant women/handmaids"; **γυναιξί** (f. dat. pl.) "with women." Penelope ascends to her upper chamber accompanied by her female servants, a typical withdrawal before she weeps for Odysseus (as the next line indicates).

lines.original: κλαῖεν ἔπειτʼ Ὀδυσῆα φίλον πόσιν, ὄφρα οἱ ὕπνον
lines.english: She wept then for Odysseus her dear husband, until upon her eyelids sweet sleep fell cast by gleaming-eyed Athena.
lines.gloss: **κλαῖεν** (imperfect, 3rd sg. of κλαίω) "she wept"; **Ὀδυσῆα** (acc. sg. of Ὀδυσσεύς) "for Odysseus," direct object; **πόσιν** (acc. sg. of πόσις) "husband," in apposition to Ὀδυσῆα; **ὄφρα** (conjunction) "until"; **ὕπνον** (acc. sg. of ὕπνος) "sleep," direct object of the verb in the next line. Penelope wept for her dear husband Odysseus until Athena cast sleep upon her eyelids.

lines.original: ἡδὺν ἐπὶ βλεφάροισι βάλε γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη.
lines.english: sweet sleep upon her eyelids cast gray-eyed Athena
lines.gloss: **ἡδὺν** (adjective, masculine accusative singular) "sweet" modifies ὕπνον from the previous line. **βλεφάροισι** (noun, neuter dative plural) "upon the eyelids" indicates where sleep is cast. **βάλε** (verb, 3rd singular aorist active indicative of βάλλω) "cast, threw" describes Athena's action. **γλαυκῶπις** (adjective, feminine nominative singular) "grey-eyed, flashing-eyed" epithetic modifier of Athena. Athena casts sweet sleep upon Penelope's eyelids, ending her weeping for Odysseus.

lines.original: μνηστῆρες δʼ ὁμάδησαν ἀνὰ μέγαρα σκιόεντα,
lines.english: The suitors raised a clamor throughout the shadowy halls.
lines.gloss: **μνηστῆρες** (nom. pl. masc., "suitors") **ὁμάδησαν** (3rd pl. aor. ind. act. of ὁμαδέω, "made uproar, shouted") **ἀνὰ** (prep. + acc., "throughout") **μέγαρα** (acc. pl. neut., "halls") **σκιόεντα** (acc. pl. neut. adj., "shadowy"). The suitors break into clamorous uproar throughout the shadowy halls, presumably reacting to Penelope's appearance or some other provocation.

lines.original: πάντες δʼ ἠρήσαντο παραὶ λεχέεσσι κλιθῆναι.
lines.english: And they all prayed to lie beside her in bed.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** πάντες (πᾶς, nominative plural masculine): "all" (subject, referring to the suitors); ἠρήσαντο (ἀράομαι, aorist middle indicative, 3rd plural): "prayed for, desired"; παραί (παρά + dative): "beside"; λεχέεσσι (λέχος, dative plural): "beds"; κλιθῆναι (κλίνω, aorist passive infinitive): "to be laid down, to recline."

All the suitors prayed to lie down beside her in bed, expressing their shared lustful desire for Penelope.

lines.original: τοῖσι δὲ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἤρχετο μύθων·
lines.english: Among them wise Telemachus began to speak.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖσι** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural): "to them," referring to the suitors.
**πεπνυμένος** (perfect middle participle, nominative singular masculine, from *πέπνυμαι*): "prudent, wise," modifying Telemachus.
**ἤρχετο** (imperfect middle, 3rd singular, from *ἄρχομαι*): "began," here with genitive μύθων meaning "began to speak."
**μύθων** (noun, genitive plural, from *μῦθος*): "of words/speech."

Telemachus, characterized as prudent, begins to address the suitors with a speech.

lines.original: ὣς ἔφαθʼ, οἱ δʼ ἄρα πάντες ὀδὰξ ἐν χείλεσι φύντες
lines.english: So he spoke, and they all bit their lips in amazement.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἔφαθʼ, οἱ δʼ ἄρα πάντες ὀδὰξ ἐν χείλεσι φύντες**

Key words: **ἔφαθʼ** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί, "he spoke"); **ὀδὰξ** (adverb, "with the teeth, biting"); **χείλεσι** (dat. pl. of χεῖλος, "lips"); **φύντες** (aor. part. nom. pl. masc. of φύω, "biting, having bitten"). "So he spoke, and they all bit their lips with their teeth"—a gesture expressing suppressed rage or frustration at Telemachus's bold speech.

lines.original: Τηλέμαχον θαύμαζον, ὃ θαρσαλέως ἀγόρευεν.
lines.english: They marveled at Telemachus, who spoke so boldly.
lines.gloss:
**Τηλέμαχον θαύμαζον, ὃ θαρσαλέως ἀγόρευεν.**

*θαύμαζον* (imperfect, 3rd pl. of θαυμάζω): "they marveled at" or "were amazed at" Telemachus. *ὃ* (relative pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "who," referring to Telemachus as subject of the relative clause. *θαρσαλέως* (adverb): "boldly" or "courageously." *ἀγόρευεν* (imperfect, 3rd sg. of ἀγορεύω): "was speaking" or "spoke." The suitors marvel at Telemachus because he speaks with unexpected boldness.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖτʼ Ἀντίνοος προσέφη, Εὐπείθεος υἱός·
lines.english: Then Antinous, son of Eupeithes, spoke to him in turn.
lines.gloss:
