**Key words:** Ἀντίνοος (nominative singular, proper name) "Antinous"; προσέφη (3rd singular aorist indicative of προσφημί) "addressed, spoke to"; Εὐπείθεος (genitive singular) "of Eupithes"; υἱός (nominative singular) "son." 

Antinous, son of Eupithes, responds to Telemachus (τὸν δʼ αὖτε = "him in turn"), likely in reaction to the bold speech that had amazed the suitors in the previous line.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: Then wise Telemachus answered him in turn.
lines.gloss:
**τὸν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·**

**τὸν** (pronoun, acc. sing. masc.) "him" – object of ηὔδα, referring to the previous speaker. **αὖ** (particle) "in turn, again" – marks speech succession. **πεπνυμένος** (perfect participle, nom. sing. masc. from πέπνυμαι) "thoughtful, prudent" – modifies Τηλέμαχος, characterizing his manner. **ἀντίον** (adverb) "in reply, face to face" – marks responsive speech. **ηὔδα** (imperfect, 3rd sing. from αὐδάω) "spoke, addressed" – main verb.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖτʼ Εὐρύμαχος Πολύβου πάϊς ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: Then Eurymachus son of Polybus answered him in turn.
lines.gloss: **Εὐρύμαχος** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Eurymachus"; **Πολύβου** (gen. sg. masc., proper name) "of Polybus"; **πάϊς** (nom. sg. masc., noun) "son"; **ἀντίον** (adv.) "in reply, in turn"; **ηὔδα** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic., *αὐδάω*) "spoke, addressed." Then Eurymachus, son of Polybus, spoke to him in reply, following the formulaic verse pattern but substituting the speaker's identity.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα·
lines.english: Then wise Telemachus answered him in turn.
lines.gloss:
**τὸν** (accusative singular masculine, demonstrative pronoun): "him," referring to Eurymachos. **αὖ** (particle): "again, in turn," marking the response. **πεπνυμένος** (nominative singular masculine, perfect middle/passive participle of *πέπνυμαι*): "prudent, wise, sensible," modifying Telemachos. **ἀντίον** (adverb): "in reply, face to face." **ηὔδα** (third singular imperfect active indicative of *αὐδάω*): "spoke, addressed." 

Telemachos, characterized as prudent, responds in turn to Eurymachos.

lines.original: ὣς φάτο Τηλέμαχος, φρεσὶ δʼ ἀθανάτην θεὸν ἔγνω.
lines.english: Thus spoke Telemachus, and in his mind he recognized the immortal goddess.
lines.gloss:
**φρεσί** (dat. pl. of φρήν): "in his mind/heart," dative of place where. **ἀθανάτην** (acc. sg. fem. of ἀθάνατος): "immortal," modifying θεόν. **θεόν** (acc. sg. of θεός): "goddess/deity," direct object of ἔγνω. **ἔγνω** (3rd sg. aor. of γιγνώσκω): "he recognized/perceived." 

Thus spoke Telemachus, and in his mind he recognized the immortal goddess (Athena departing in disguise).

lines.original: οἱ δʼ εἰς ὀρχηστύν τε καὶ ἱμερόεσσαν ἀοιδὴν
lines.english: They turned to dance and lovely song and took their pleasure, waiting for evening to come.
lines.gloss:
**οἱ δʼ** (nom. pl. masc. article + particle): "and they"
**ὀρχηστύν** (acc. sg. fem.): "dancing," object of εἰς
**ἱμερόεσσαν** (acc. sg. fem. adj.): "lovely, delightful," modifying ἀοιδήν
**ἀοιδήν** (acc. sg. fem.): "song," coordinated with ὀρχηστύν as objects of εἰς

The suitors turn to dancing and delightful song after Telemachus's recognition of Athena.

lines.original: τρεψάμενοι τέρποντο, μένον δʼ ἐπὶ ἕσπερον ἐλθεῖν.
lines.english: They turned to dancing and delightful song and took their pleasure, waiting for evening to come.
lines.gloss: **τρεψάμενοι** (aorist middle participle, nominative plural, from τρέπω) "having turned (themselves)," refers to turning their attention to dance and song. **τέρποντο** (imperfect middle, 3rd plural, from τέρπω) "they were delighting themselves, taking pleasure." **μένον** (imperfect active, 3rd plural, from μένω) "they waited, remained." **ἕσπερον** (accusative masculine singular) "evening," the object of waiting. **ἐλθεῖν** (aorist active infinitive, from ἔρχομαι) "to come," expressing purpose or result of their waiting.

lines.original: τοῖσι δὲ τερπομένοισι μέλας ἐπὶ ἕσπερος ἦλθε·
lines.english: And as they were making merry, dark evening came upon them.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖσι** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "for them," referring to those enjoying themselves.

**τερπομένοισι** (τέρπω, present middle participle, dative plural masculine): "enjoying themselves," describing their state of pleasure.

**μέλας** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "dark," modifying evening.

**ἕσπερος** (noun, nominative singular masculine): "evening," the subject of the verb.

**ἦλθε** (ἔρχομαι, aorist active indicative, 3rd singular): "came," indicating evening's arrival.

While they were enjoying themselves, dark evening came upon them.

lines.original: δὴ τότε κακκείοντες ἔβαν οἶκόνδε ἕκαστος.
lines.english: Then they went off to bed, each one to his own home.
lines.gloss: **δή** (particle): emphasizing "then indeed"; **τότε** (adverb): "then, at that time"; **κακκείοντες** (present participle, nominative plural masculine of κατακοιμάω): "lying down to sleep, going to bed"; **ἔβαν** (3rd plural aorist indicative of βαίνω): "they went"; **οἶκόνδε** (adverb): "homeward, to their homes"; **ἕκαστος** (nominative singular masculine): "each one." Then indeed each one went homeward to bed, dispersing after the evening's entertainment.

lines.original: Τηλέμαχος δʼ, ὅθι οἱ θάλαμος περικαλλέος αὐλῆς
lines.english: Telemachus, where his chamber in the very beautiful courtyard
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** Τηλέμαχος (nom. sg. masc., proper name, "Telemachus"); θάλαμος (nom. sg. masc., "chamber, bedroom"); περικαλλέος (gen. sg. fem., "very beautiful," compound adj. with περι- intensive); αὐλῆς (gen. sg. fem., "courtyard, enclosed space").

Telemachus's sleeping chamber is located in the very beautiful courtyard; the genitive περικαλλέος αὐλῆς depends on θάλαμος, indicating the chamber's position within or adjoining the splendid courtyard.

lines.original: ὑψηλὸς δέδμητο περισκέπτῳ ἐνὶ χώρῳ,
lines.english: was built high up in a conspicuous place in the precinct
lines.gloss:
**ὑψηλὸς** (adj., nom. sg. masc.) "lofty, high up" - modifies θάλαμος from the previous line. **δέδμητο** (pluperfect passive indic., 3rd sg.) "had been built" from δέμω. **περισκέπτῳ** (adj., dat. sg. masc./neut.) "visible all around, commanding a view" - compounds περι- + σκέπτομαι. **χώρῳ** (noun, dat. sg. masc.) "place, spot" - locative dative indicating where the chamber was built.

This line continues the description of Telemachus' bedroom, emphasizing it was built in an elevated location with views all around the courtyard.

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ἔβη εἰς εὐνὴν πολλὰ φρεσὶ μερμηρίζων.
lines.english: There he went to bed pondering many things in his heart.
lines.gloss:
**ἔνθα** (adverb): "there, thither" — indicating the destination of movement.
**ἔβη** (3rd sg. aorist indic. act. of βαίνω): "he went" — describing Odysseus's action.
**εὐνήν** (acc. sg. fem. of εὐνή): "bed, resting-place" — the goal of his movement.
**φρεσί** (dat. pl. of φρήν): "in his mind/heart" — locative dative indicating the seat of thought.
**μερμηρίζων** (pres. part. masc. nom. sg. of μερμηρίζω): "pondering, deliberating" — describing his mental state while going to bed.

lines.original: τῷ δʼ ἄρʼ ἅμʼ αἰθομένας δαΐδας φέρε κεδνὰ ἰδυῖα
lines.english: And with him a wise and loyal servant carried blazing torches.
lines.gloss: **τῷ** (dat. sing. masc., "for him"), **ἅμα** (adv., "along with"), **αἰθομένας** (pres. part. acc. pl. fem. from αἴθω, "blazing/burning"), **δαΐδας** (acc. pl. fem., "torches"), **φέρε** (3rd sing. impf. from φέρω, "was carrying"), **κεδνά** (nom. sing. fem., "faithful/devoted"), **ἰδυῖα** (perf. part. nom. sing. fem. from οἶδα, "knowing/skilled"). The faithful servant, skilled in her duties, carried blazing torches along with him.

lines.original: Εὐρύκλειʼ, Ὦπος θυγάτηρ Πεισηνορίδαο,
lines.english: Eurycleia, daughter of Ops son of Peisenor
lines.gloss: The line introduces Eurycleia with her patronymic. **Εὐρύκλειʼ** (nominative singular, proper name) "Eurycleia," the loyal household servant; **θυγάτηρ** (nominative singular, noun) "daughter"; **Ὦπος** (genitive singular, proper name) "of Ops"; **Πεισηνορίδαο** (genitive singular, patronymic adjective) "son of Peisenor," further specifying Ops's lineage. The double patronymic emphasizes Eurycleia's respectable family origins despite her enslaved status.

lines.original: τήν ποτε Λαέρτης πρίατο κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν
lines.english: whom Laertes once bought with his own possessions
lines.gloss:
**τήν** (demonstrative pronoun, feminine accusative singular) "her" refers back to Eurycleia. **ποτε** (enclitic adverb) "once, at one time." **Λαέρτης** (proper noun, nominative singular) "Laertes," Odysseus' father, subject of the verb. **πρίατο** (verb, 3rd singular aorist middle indicative of πρίαμαι) "bought, purchased." **κτεάτεσσιν** (noun, neuter dative plural of κτέας) "with possessions, with his wealth" - instrumental dative. 

Laertes once purchased Eurycleia with his own wealth when she was still in her youth.

lines.original: πρωθήβην ἔτʼ ἐοῦσαν, ἐεικοσάβοια δʼ ἔδωκεν,
lines.english: when she was in the first bloom of youth, and he gave twenty oxen for her
lines.gloss: **πρωθήβην** (acc. sg. fem., "in first youth/prime of life") **ἔτʼ** = ἔτι (adv., "still, yet") **ἐοῦσαν** (pres. part. acc. sg. fem. εἰμί, "being") **ἐεικοσάβοια** (acc. pl. neut., "worth twenty oxen") **ἔδωκεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. δίδωμι, "he gave"). Laertes purchased her when she was still in the bloom of youth, and he gave [goods] worth twenty oxen as her price.

lines.original: ἶσα δέ μιν κεδνῇ ἀλόχῳ τίεν ἐν μεγάροισιν,
lines.english: He honored her equally with his true wife in the halls.
lines.gloss: **ἶσα** (adverb): "equally," modifying **τίεν**. **κεδνῇ ἀλόχῳ** (dative singular feminine adjective + noun): "to his wedded wife," dative of comparison. **τίεν** (3rd singular imperfect active of τίω): "he honored." **μεγάροισιν** (dative plural neuter): "in the halls." He honored her equally to his wedded wife in the household, despite never sharing her bed.

lines.original: εὐνῇ δʼ οὔ ποτʼ ἔμικτο, χόλον δʼ ἀλέεινε γυναικός·
lines.english: He never shared her bed, but avoided the woman's anger.
lines.gloss:
**Glossary for Odyssey line: εὐνῇ δʼ οὔ ποτʼ ἔμικτο, χόλον δʼ ἀλέεινε γυναικός·**

- **εὐνῇ** (dative singular of εὐνή): "bed," dative of respect or place where
- **ἔμικτο** (3rd singular aorist middle indicative of μίγνυμι): "he mingled/had intercourse," here negated by οὔ ποτε ("never")
- **χόλον** (accusative singular of χόλος): "anger, wrath," direct object of ἀλέεινε
- **ἀλέεινε** (3rd singular imperfect active of ἀλεείνω): "he was avoiding, shunning

lines.original: ἥ οἱ ἅμʼ αἰθομένας δαΐδας φέρε, καί ἑ μάλιστα
lines.english: She carried blazing torches for him and loved him most of all the servants.
lines.gloss: **ἥ** (relative pronoun, nom. fem. sing.) "who"; **αἰθομένας** (pres. mid./pass. participle, acc. fem. pl. from αἴθω) "blazing, burning"; **δαΐδας** (acc. fem. pl.) "torches"; **φέρε** (imperf. 3rd sing. from φέρω) "was carrying"; **μάλιστα** (adverb, superlative) "most of all, especially." She who was carrying blazing torches for him, and loved him most of all (among the servants).

lines.original: δμῳάων φιλέεσκε, καὶ ἔτρεφε τυτθὸν ἐόντα.
lines.english: She loved him most of all the servants and had nursed him when he was small.
lines.gloss:
**δμῳάων** (gen. pl. fem. of δμῳή): "of the maidservants/female slaves"
**φιλέεσκε** (3rd sg. impf. iterative of φιλέω): "she used to love/cherish (habitually)"
**ἔτρεφε** (3rd sg. impf. of τρέφω): "she reared/nurtured"
**τυτθὸν ἐόντα** (acc. sg. masc. part. of εἰμί with adj. τυτθός): "him being small/a little child"

She habitually loved him among the maidservants and nurtured him when he was a small child.

lines.original: ὤιξεν δὲ θύρας θαλάμου πύκα ποιητοῖο,
lines.english: She opened the doors of the well-built storeroom.
lines.gloss: **ὤιξεν** (ἀνοίγω, aorist active indicative, 3rd singular): "opened" — describes Eurycleia opening the door. **θύρας** (θύρα, accusative plural feminine): "doors" — direct object, the double doors being opened. **θαλάμου** (θάλαμος, genitive singular masculine): "of the storeroom/chamber" — defines which doors. **πύκα ποιητοῖο** (πυκνός/πύκα + ποιητός, adverb + genitive singular masculine): "closely/well built" — describes the craftsmanship of the chamber.

lines.original: ἕζετο δʼ ἐν λέκτρῳ, μαλακὸν δʼ ἔκδυνε χιτῶνα·
lines.english: She sat on the bed and took off her soft tunic.
lines.gloss:
**ἕζετο** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ἕζομαι): "he sat down"
**λέκτρῳ** (noun, dat. sg. neut. of λέκτρον): "on the bed"
**μαλακὸν** (adj, acc. sg. masc. of μαλακός): "soft"
**ἔκδυνε** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἐκδύω): "he took off"
**χιτῶνα** (noun, acc. sg. masc. of χιτών): "tunic"

Odysseus sat down on the bed and removed his soft tunic, preparing for rest.

lines.original: καὶ τὸν μὲν γραίης πυκιμηδέος ἔμβαλε χερσίν.
lines.english: And she placed it in the hands of the wise old woman.
lines.gloss:
**γραίης** (gen. sg. fem. of γραῖα): "old woman's," genitive depending on χερσίν. **πυκιμηδέος** (gen. sg. fem. of πυκιμηδής): "wise-counseled, shrewd," compound epithet modifying γραίης. **ἔμβαλε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἐμβάλλω): "she placed into," governs dative χερσίν. **χερσίν** (dat. pl. fem. of χείρ): "into the hands," dative of place where.

The subject (Odysseus) placed the tunic into the hands of the shrewd old woman (Eurycleia).

lines.original: ἡ μὲν τὸν πτύξασα καὶ ἀσκήσασα χιτῶνα,
lines.english: She folded and smoothed the tunic
lines.gloss:
**ἡ μὲν τὸν πτύξασα καὶ ἀσκήσασα χιτῶνα,**

Key words: **πτύξασα** (aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. fem., πτύσσω) "having folded"; **ἀσκήσασα** (aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. fem., ἀσκέω) "having smoothed/dressed"; **χιτῶνα** (acc. sg. masc., χιτών) "tunic/shirt." The old woman (subject of ἡ μέν) folds and smooths Odysseus's garment before hanging it on the peg (next line).

lines.original: πασσάλῳ ἀγκρεμάσασα παρὰ τρητοῖσι λέχεσσι
lines.english: hanging it on a peg beside the inlaid bed
lines.gloss: **πασσάλῳ** (dat. sing. masc. of πάσσαλος): "on a peg," dative of place where. **ἀγκρεμάσασα** (aor. act. ptc. nom. sing. fem. of ἀνακρεμάννυμι): "having hung up," modifying the implied subject (Penelope). **παρά** (prep. + dat.): "beside." **τρητοῖσι** (dat. pl. neut. of τρητός): "perforated, bored-through," describing **λέχεσσι** (dat. pl. neut. of λέχος): "bedposts." She hangs the folded garment on a peg beside the ornately worked bedframe.

lines.original: βῆ ῥʼ ἴμεν ἐκ θαλάμοιο, θύρην δʼ ἐπέρυσσε κορώνῃ
lines.english: She went from the chamber and drew the door shut with the curved handle.
lines.gloss: **βῆ** (3rd sg. aorist of βαίνω): "she went"; **ἴμεν** (infinitive of εἶμι): "to go"; **θαλάμοιο** (genitive singular of θάλαμος): "from the chamber"; **ἐπέρυσσε** (3rd sg. imperfect of ἐπερύω): "she pulled to/shut"; **κορώνῃ** (dative singular of κορώνη): "with the curved handle." She departed from the chamber and pulled the door shut by its curved handle.

lines.original: ἀργυρέῃ, ἐπὶ δὲ κληῖδʼ ἐτάνυσσεν ἱμάντι.
lines.english: with a silver handle, and she drew the bolt across with a strap.
lines.gloss:
**ἀργυρέῃ** (adj., dat. sing. fem., "silver"): modifies κορώνῃ from the previous line, describing the silver hook or handle of the door. **ἐπὶ δέ** (prep. + particle, "and moreover/upon"): introduces the additional action of securing the door with the key. **κληῖδʼ** (noun, acc. sing. fem., "key"): the object being extended or drawn through. **ἐτάνυσσεν** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. indic. act., "she stretched/extended"): describes pulling the key through on its strap. **ἱμάντι** (noun, dat. sing. masc., "thong/strap"): the leather strap attached to the key, instrumental dative.

Penelope closes the door with a silver hook and secures it by drawing

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ὅ γε παννύχιος, κεκαλυμμένος οἰὸς ἀώτῳ,
lines.english: There he lay all night long, covered with fine fleece alone, pondering in his mind the path Athena had shown him.
lines.gloss:
**παννύχιος** (adj., nom. sg. masc.): "all night long," "throughout the night." **κεκαλυμμένος** (perf. mid./pass. part., nom. sg. masc. of καλύπτω): "covered," "wrapped." **οἰός** (nom. sg. masc. of ὄϊς): "fleece," referring to a sheep's wool. **ἀώτῳ** (dat. sg. of ἄωτον): "finest wool" or "choice fleece."

There he lay all night long, covered in/with choice fleece.

lines.original: βούλευε φρεσὶν ᾗσιν ὁδὸν τὴν πέφραδʼ Ἀθήνη.
lines.english: He pondered in his heart the way that Athena had shown him.
lines.gloss:
**βούλευε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of βουλεύω): "he was pondering/deliberating"
**φρεσὶν ᾗσιν** (dat. pl. fem. of φρήν + possessive adj.): "in his own mind/heart" 
**ὁδὸν τὴν** (acc. sg. fem. of ὁδός + article): "the way/course"
**πέφραδʼ** (3rd sg. plupf. act. indic. of φράζω, elided): "had shown/indicated"
**Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg. fem.): "Athena" (subject of πέφραδε)

The hero was deliberating in his mind the course of action that Athena had shown him.

lines.original: ὢ πόποι, οἷον δή νυ θεοὺς βροτοὶ αἰτιόωνται·
lines.english: Alas, how mortals blame the gods for their troubles!
lines.gloss:
**ὢ πόποι** (interjection): exclamation of surprise or indignation, "alas, oh my!" **οἷον** (relative pronoun, acc. sg. neut.): "how much" or "what sort of things." **θεοὺς** (noun, acc. pl. masc.): "gods," object of αἰτιόωνται. **βροτοὶ** (noun, nom. pl. masc.): "mortals," subject of the verb. **αἰτιόωνται** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. mid. indic.): "they blame" or "they hold responsible." 

Zeus laments that mortals blame the gods for their troubles, introducing a key theme of human responsibility for suffering.

lines.original: ἐξ ἡμέων γάρ φασι κάκʼ ἔμμεναι, οἱ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ
lines.english: For they say that evils come from us, but they themselves through their own recklessness have pains beyond their fate.
lines.gloss: **ἐξ ἡμέων** (prep. + gen. pronoun, 1st pl.): "from us" – the gods as source of evils in mortal perception. **φασι** (3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of φημί): "they say/claim" – mortals assert this blame. **κάκʼ** (neut. pl. acc. of κακόν, crasis for κακά): "evils" – the misfortunes mortals attribute to divine causation. **ἔμμεναι** (pres. act. inf. of εἰμί): "to be" – completes the indirect statement. Zeus complains that mortals blame the gods for evils that actually come from their own recklessness.

lines.original: σφῇσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν ὑπὲρ μόρον ἄλγεʼ ἔχουσιν,
lines.english: through their own recklessness they have pains beyond their fate
lines.gloss:
**σφῇσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν ὑπὲρ μόρον ἄλγεʼ ἔχουσιν**

**σφῇσιν** (possessive adjective, dat. pl. fem.): "by their own"; **ἀτασθαλίῃσιν** (noun, dat. pl. fem.): "through reckless folly/transgressions"; **ὑπὲρ μόρον** (prep. + acc.): "beyond fate/destiny"; **ἄλγεʼ** (ἄλγεα, noun, acc. pl. neut.): "woes, sufferings"; **ἔχουσιν** (ἔχω, 3rd pl. pres. act. ind.): "they have." Mortals suffer

lines.original: ὡς καὶ νῦν Αἴγισθος ὑπὲρ μόρον Ἀτρεΐδαο
lines.english: So now Aegisthus beyond his fate wooed the wife of Atrides' son
lines.gloss: **ὡς** (adverb): "thus, so" — introduces a comparison with the preceding gnomic statement. **νῦν** (adverb): "now" — marks the specific recent example. **Αἴγισθος** (proper noun, nominative singular): Aegisthus, the paradigmatic transgressor. **ὑπὲρ μόρον** (prepositional phrase): "beyond fate/destiny" — the key formula indicating exceeding one's allotted portion through recklessness. **Ἀτρεΐδαο** (proper noun, genitive singular): "of the son of Atreus" (Agamemnon) — the victim whose wife Aegisthus married.

lines.original: γῆμʼ ἄλοχον μνηστήν, τὸν δʼ ἔκτανε νοστήσαντα,
lines.english: He married the wedded wife and killed him when he returned home.
lines.gloss:
**γῆμʼ** (γῆμε, aorist active indicative 3rd sg. of γαμέω) "married"; **ἄλοχον** (accusative sg. feminine) "wife"; **μνηστήν** (accusative sg. feminine adjective) "wedded, courted"; **ἔκτανε** (aorist active indicative 3rd sg. of κτείνω) "killed, slew"; **νοστήσαντα** (aorist active participle accusative sg. masculine of νοστέω) "returning home, having returned."

Aegisthus married the wedded wife and killed (Agamemnon) upon his return home—a paradigmatic violation committed despite divine warning.

lines.original: εἰδὼς αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον, ἐπεὶ πρό οἱ εἴπομεν ἡμεῖς,
lines.english: knowing his sheer destruction, since we had warned him beforehand,
lines.gloss: **εἰδὼς** (perfect active participle, nominative singular masculine, from *οἶδα*) "knowing" modifies the subject (Aegisthus), indicating his awareness. **αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον** "sheer/steep destruction" (accusative singular, object of εἰδώς). **ἐπεί** "since" introduces causal clause. **πρό** adverb "beforehand." **εἴπομεν** (aorist active indicative, 1st plural, from *εἶπον*) "we told/spoke." The line emphasizes Aegisthus acted knowingly despite divine warning of his doom.

lines.original: Ἑρμείαν πέμψαντες, ἐύσκοπον ἀργεϊφόντην,
lines.english: having sent Hermes, the keen-sighted slayer of Argus,
lines.gloss: **Ἑρμείαν** (acc. sg. masc., Hermes) "Hermes"; **πέμψαντες** (aor. act. ptcp. nom. pl. masc. of πέμπω) "having sent"; **ἐύσκοπον** (acc. sg. masc. adj.) "the keen-sighted watchman"; **ἀργεϊφόντην** (acc. sg. masc. epithet) "slayer of Argus." The gods sent Hermes, the vigilant slayer of Argus, to warn against the crime.

lines.original: μήτʼ αὐτὸν κτείνειν μήτε μνάασθαι ἄκοιτιν·
lines.english: neither to kill him himself nor to woo his wife
lines.gloss:
**μήτʼ αὐτὸν κτείνειν μήτε μνάασθαι ἄκοιτιν·**

Key words: **μήτε** (conjunction, "neither...nor"), **κτείνειν** (present active infinitive of κτείνω, "to kill"), **μνάασθαι** (present middle infinitive of μνάομαι, "to woo, court"), **ἄκοιτιν** (accusative singular feminine of ἄκοιτις, "wife, spouse"). The gods warn Aegisthus neither to kill Agamemnon nor to court his wife Clytemnestra.

lines.original: ἐκ γὰρ Ὀρέσταο τίσις ἔσσεται Ἀτρεΐδαο,
lines.english: For vengeance will come from Orestes son of Atreus
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἐκ (preposition + genitive) "from"; Ὀρέσταο (genitive singular of Ὀρέστης) "of/from Orestes"; τίσις (nominative singular noun) "vengeance, retribution"; ἔσσεται (future middle/passive 3rd singular of εἰμί) "will be"; Ἀτρεΐδαο (genitive singular of Ἀτρεΐδης) "of the son of Atreus" (i.e., Agamemnon). 

The line warns that vengeance will come from Orestes, son of Agamemnon (the Atreides), foreshadowing the famous mythological revenge for his father's murder.

lines.original: ὁππότʼ ἂν ἡβήσῃ τε καὶ ἧς ἱμείρεται αἴης.
lines.english: whenever he reaches manhood and longs for his own land.
lines.gloss:
**ὁππότε** (ὁππότε ἄν): temporal conjunction with modal particle, "whenever, when"
**ἡβήσῃ** (ἡβάω): 3rd sing. aor. subj., "he reaches manhood, comes of age"
**ἧς**: fem. gen. sing. of possessive adjective ὅς, "his own"
**ἱμείρεται** (ἱμείρομαι): 3rd sing. pres. mid. indic., "he longs for, desires"
**αἴης** (αἶα): gen. sing., "land, homeland"

The line describes the time when Orestes will reach maturity and yearn for his native land, setting the conditions for his eventual vengeance.

lines.original: ὣς ἔφαθʼ Ἑρμείας, ἀλλʼ οὐ φρένας Αἰγίσθοιο
lines.english: Thus spoke Hermes, but he did not persuade the mind of Aegisthus.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἔφαθʼ Ἑρμείας, ἀλλʼ οὐ φρένας Αἰγίσθοιο**

*ὣς* (adverb): "thus, in this way"; *ἔφαθʼ* (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί): "he spoke," referring to Hermes' warning; *Ἑρμείας* (nom. sg.): "Hermes," subject; *φρένας* (acc. pl. of φρήν): "mind, wits" (object of implied verb of persuasion); *Αἰγίσθοιο* (gen. sg.): "of Aegisthus," possessive genitive. Thus Hermes spoke, but he did not persuade the mind of Aegisthus.

lines.original: πεῖθʼ ἀγαθὰ φρονέων· νῦν δʼ ἁθρόα πάντʼ ἀπέτισεν.
lines.english: He spoke with good intent, but did not persuade him, and now he has paid for everything together.
lines.gloss: **πεῖθʼ** (πείθω): 3rd sg. imperfect active, "he persuaded" or "was persuading." **ἀγαθὰ φρονέων**: present participle masculine nominative, "thinking good things" or "being well-intentioned." **ἁθρόα**: adverb, "all together" or "collectively." **ἀπέτισεν**: 3rd sg. aorist active (ἀποτίνω), "he paid back" or "suffered the penalty." Hermes failed to persuade Aegisthus despite offering good counsel; now Aegisthus has paid the full price all at once for his crimes.

lines.original: ὦ πάτερ ἡμέτερε Κρονίδη, ὕπατε κρειόντων,
lines.english: O father of ours, son of Kronos, highest of rulers
lines.gloss:
**ὦ πάτερ ἡμέτερε Κρονίδη, ὕπατε κρειόντων**

**πάτερ** (nom. sg., vocative usage): "father"; **ἡμέτερε** (voc. sg. masc.): "our"; **Κρονίδη** (voc. sg.): "son of Kronos," epithet of Zeus; **ὕπατε** (voc. sg. superlative adj.): "highest, supreme"; **κρειόντων** (gen. pl. pres. participle of κραίνω): "of rulers/lords." Telemachus addresses Zeus with accumulating vocatives, invoking him as "our father, son of Kronos, highest of all rulers."

lines.original: καὶ λίην κεῖνός γε ἐοικότι κεῖται ὀλέθρῳ·
lines.english: And truly that man lies in a fitting destruction.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 
- **λίην** (adverb): "very much, exceedingly"
- **κεῖνός** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.): "that man" (= ἐκεῖνος, referring to Aegisthus)
- **ἐοικότι** (perfect active participle, dat. sg. neut. from ἔοικα): "fitting, appropriate"
- **κεῖται** (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass. of κεῖμαι): "lies (dead)"
- **ὀλέθρῳ** (noun, dat. sg. masc.): "destruction, death"

Athena affirms that Aegisthus lies dead in a thoroughly fitting destruction, emphasizing the appropriateness of his doom as punishment for his crimes.

lines.original: ὡς ἀπόλοιτο καὶ ἄλλος, ὅτις τοιαῦτά γε ῥέζοι·
lines.english: So may anyone else perish who does such deeds.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ὡς (adverb) "thus, so"; ἀπόλοιτο (3rd sing. aorist optative middle of ἀπόλλυμι) "may he perish"; ἄλλος (nominative singular masculine adjective) "another"; ὅστις (relative pronoun, nominative singular) "whoever"; ῥέζοι (3rd sing. present optative active of ῥέζω) "should do, might do."

Athena expresses a wish that anyone else who acts in such a way should likewise perish, using optatives to convey her desired outcome for would-be wrongdoers.

lines.original: ἀλλά μοι ἀμφʼ Ὀδυσῆι δαΐφρονι δαίεται ἦτορ,
lines.english: But my heart is consumed with grief for Odysseus of the nimble mind.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλά** (strong adversative conjunction) "but": marks transition from Aegisthus to Odysseus. **ἀμφ(ί)** (preposition + dative) "about, concerning": with Ὀδυσῆι. **δαΐφρονι** (adjective, dative singular masculine) "god-like in counsel, resourceful": epithet modifying Ὀδυσῆι. **δαίεται** (present indicative middle, 3rd singular) "is burned, is consumed": from δαίω. **ἦτορ** (noun, nominative singular neuter) "heart": subject of the verb, expressing Zeus's concern.

Zeus shifts from condemning Aegisthus to expressing his burning concern for the suffering, resourceful Odysseus.

lines.original: δυσμόρῳ, ὃς δὴ δηθὰ φίλων ἄπο πήματα πάσχει
lines.english: the ill-fated one who has long been suffering woes far from his loved ones
lines.gloss: **δυσμόρῳ** (adjective, dative singular masculine): "ill-fated, wretched," modifying Odysseus from the previous line. **δηθὰ** (adverb): "for a long time, long since." **φίλων** (adjective/substantive, genitive plural): "dear ones, loved ones, friends/family," indicating separation. **ἄπο** (preposition with genitive, anastrophe of ἀπό): "away from, far from." **πήματα** (noun, accusative plural neuter): "sufferings, woes." The line describes Odysseus as wretched, suffering woes for a long time away from his loved ones.

lines.original: νήσῳ ἐν ἀμφιρύτῃ, ὅθι τʼ ὀμφαλός ἐστι θαλάσσης.
lines.english: on a sea-girt island, where lies the navel of the sea.
lines.gloss: **νήσῳ** (dative singular of νῆσος): "on an island"; **ἀμφιρύτῃ** (dative singular feminine adjective): "sea-girt, surrounded by water"; **ὀμφαλός** (nominative singular): "navel, center"; **θαλάσσης** (genitive singular of θάλασσα): "of the sea." The hero suffers on a sea-girt island which is the navel or center-point of the sea, emphasizing his extreme isolation at the world's heart.

lines.original: νῆσος δενδρήεσσα, θεὰ δʼ ἐν δώματα ναίει,
lines.english: A wooded island, and a goddess dwells there in her halls.
lines.gloss: **νῆσος** (nom. sg. fem., "island") is the subject. **δενδρήεσσα** (nom. sg. fem., adj., "wooded, tree-covered") describes the island. **θεὰ** (nom. sg. fem., "goddess") is the subject of the second clause. **δώματα** (acc. pl. neut., "dwelling, house") indicates where the goddess dwells. **ναίει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic., "dwells, inhabits") is the main verb of the second clause. The line describes Calypso's wooded island and notes that a goddess dwells in the dwelling there.

lines.original: Ἄτλαντος θυγάτηρ ὀλοόφρονος, ὅς τε θαλάσσης
lines.english: the daughter of Atlas of baneful mind, who knows the depths of all the sea
lines.gloss:
**Ἄτλαντος θυγάτηρ ὀλοόφρονος, ὅς τε θαλάσσης**

**Ἄτλαντος** (gen. sg. masc. of Ἄτλας): "of Atlas," genitive of possession modifying θυγάτηρ. **θυγάτηρ** (nom. sg. fem.): "daughter," subject identifying Calypso. **ὀλοόφρονος** (gen. sg. masc. of ὀλοόφρων): "destructive-minded, baneful," epithet modifying Ἄτλαντος. **ὅς** (nom. sg. masc. relative pronoun): "who," referring back to Atlas. The line identifies Calypso as the daughter of destructive-minded Atlas, who (as the

lines.original: πάσης βένθεα οἶδεν, ἔχει δέ τε κίονας αὐτὸς
lines.english: who knows the depths of all the sea and himself holds the tall pillars
lines.gloss:
**πάσης** (πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν): genitive singular feminine, "of all," modifying θαλάσσης from the previous line. **βένθεα** (βένθος, -εος, τό): accusative plural neuter, "depths." **οἶδεν** (οἶδα): third singular perfect with present meaning, "he knows." **κίονας** (κίων, -ονος, ὁ): accusative plural masculine, "pillars." **αὐτὸς**: nominative singular masculine intensive pronoun, "himself," emphasizing the subject (Atlas). 

Atlas himself knows the depths of all the sea and holds the pillars that keep earth and heaven apart.

lines.original: μακράς, αἳ γαῖάν τε καὶ οὐρανὸν ἀμφὶς ἔχουσιν.
lines.english: long ones which hold the earth and heaven apart on both sides
lines.gloss: **μακράς** (adj., acc. fem. pl.) "long," modifying κίονας from the previous line; **γαῖάν** (noun, acc. fem. sg.) "earth," object of ἔχουσιν; **οὐρανὸν** (noun, acc. masc. sg.) "heaven/sky," also object of ἔχουσιν; **ἀμφὶς** (adv.) "apart, asunder"; **ἔχουσιν** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. act. indic.) "hold, keep." The long pillars hold earth and heaven apart, continuing the description of Atlas's cosmic role.

lines.original: τοῦ θυγάτηρ δύστηνον ὀδυρόμενον κατερύκει,
lines.english: His daughter detains him as he grieves wretchedly.
lines.gloss: **τοῦ** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive singular masculine) "of him/his" — refers to Atlas from the previous line. **θυγάτηρ** (noun, nominative singular feminine) "daughter" — Calypso, Atlas's daughter. **δύστηνον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine) "wretched, unhappy" — modifies Odysseus. **ὀδυρόμενον** (verb, present middle participle, accusative singular masculine) "lamenting, grieving" — describes Odysseus's state. **κατερύκει** (verb, third person singular present active indicative) "detains, holds back" — Calypso's action of keeping Odysseus on her island.

lines.original: αἰεὶ δὲ μαλακοῖσι καὶ αἱμυλίοισι λόγοισιν
lines.english: and she constantly beguiles him with soft and wheedling words
lines.gloss:
**αἰεὶ** (adverb) "always, constantly" - marks the persistence of Calypso's efforts.

**μαλακοῖσι** (adjective, dative plural masculine/neuter, from μαλακός) "soft, gentle, beguiling" - describes the seductive nature of her words.

**αἱμυλίοισι** (adjective, dative plural masculine/neuter, from αἱμύλιος) "flattering, wheedling, cunning" - emphasizes the crafty persuasiveness of her speech.

**λόγοισιν** (noun, dative plural, from λόγος) "with words, speeches" - instrumental dative showing the means of enchantment.

Calypso continually employs soft and cunning words to enchant Odysseus, attempting to make him forget Ithaca.

lines.original: θέλγει, ὅπως Ἰθάκης ἐπιλήσεται· αὐτὰρ Ὀδυσσεύς,
lines.english: He beguiles him so that he may forget Ithaca, but Odysseus,
lines.gloss: **θέλγει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of θέλγω) "enchants, beguiles"; **ὅπως** (conjunction) "so that, in order that"; **ἐπιλήσεται** (3rd sg. fut. mid. indic. of ἐπιλανθάνομαι) "he may forget" (+ gen.); **Ἰθάκης** (gen. sg. of Ἰθάκη) "of Ithaca"; **Ὀδυσσεύς** (nom. sg.) "Odysseus." Calypso enchants Odysseus with soft and wheedling words so that he will forget Ithaca, but Odysseus (in contrast) continues to long for home.

lines.original: ἱέμενος καὶ καπνὸν ἀποθρῴσκοντα νοῆσαι
lines.english: yearning even to see the smoke rising up from his own land
lines.gloss:
**ἱέμενος** (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc., from ἵεμαι): "desiring, longing"
**καπνόν** (acc. sg. masc. noun): "smoke"
**ἀποθρῴσκοντα** (pres. act. participle, acc. sg. masc., from ἀποθρῴσκω): "leaping up, rising"
**νοῆσαι** (aor. inf. act., from νοέω): "to perceive, to see"

Odysseus longs even to see the smoke rising from his homeland (Ithaca), expressing his intense yearning for home despite Calypso's enchantment.

lines.original: ἧς γαίης, θανέειν ἱμείρεται. οὐδέ νυ σοί περ
lines.english: of his own land, he longs to die. Yet not even you care in your heart, Olympian.
lines.gloss:
**ἧς γαίης, θανέειν ἱμείρεται. οὐδέ νυ σοί περ**

Key words: **ἧς** (relative pronoun, genitive singular feminine, "of which"); **γαίης** (noun, genitive singular, "of land/earth"); **θανέειν** (verb, aorist active infinitive, "to die"); **ἱμείρεται** (verb, 3rd singular present middle, "he desires/longs"); **σοί** (pronoun, dative singular, "to you"). Athena tells Zeus that Odysseus longs to die rather than remain away from his homeland, and that even Zeus's heart is not moved by this suffering.

lines.original: ἐντρέπεται φίλον ἦτορ, Ὀλύμπιε. οὔ νύ τʼ Ὀδυσσεὺς
lines.english: Your heart is not moved, Olympian, yet Odysseus once pleased you.
lines.gloss: **ἐντρέπεται** (3rd sg. pres. mid. indic. of ἐντρέπομαι) "is moved, feels respect/pity"; **φίλον** (acc. sg. neut. of φίλος) "dear, own"; **ἦτορ** (acc. sg. neut.) "heart"; **Ὀλύμπιε** (voc. sg. masc. of Ὀλύμπιος) "Olympian (one)"; **Ὀδυσσεύς** (nom. sg.) "Odysseus." Athena asks Zeus why his heart is not moved with pity for Odysseus, addressing him as "Olympian," followed by the emphatic statement that Odysseus performed sacrifices.

lines.original: Ἀργείων παρὰ νηυσὶ χαρίζετο ἱερὰ ῥέζων
lines.english: Did not Odysseus please you beside the Argive ships when he was offering sacrifices in broad Troy?
lines.gloss:
**Ἀργείων παρὰ νηυσὶ χαρίζετο ἱερὰ ῥέζων**

*Ἀργείων* (gen. pl., Ἀργεῖοι) "of the Argives"; *παρὰ νηυσί* (dat. pl., ναῦς) "beside the ships"; *χαρίζετο* (3rd sg. impf. mid., χαρίζομαι) "was he showing favor, gratifying"; *ἱερά* (acc. pl. neut., ἱερόν) "sacrifices, sacred rites"; *ῥέζων* (pres. part. nom. sg. masc., ῥέζω) "performing, making." Athena asks Zeus why Odysseus found no favor despite performing sacrifices by the

lines.original: Τροίῃ ἐν εὐρείῃ; τί νύ οἱ τόσον ὠδύσαο, Ζεῦ;
lines.english: In wide Troy; why then have you been so wrathful against him, Zeus?
lines.gloss:
**Τροίῃ ἐν εὐρείῃ; τί νύ οἱ τόσον ὠδύσαο, Ζεῦ;**

**Τροίῃ** (dat. sg. fem., "Τροίη"): "in Troy," locative dative with preposition ἐν. **εὐρείῃ** (dat. sg. fem., "εὐρύς"): "wide, broad," agreeing with Τροίῃ. **ὠδύσαο** (2nd sg. aor. mid. indic., "ὀδύσσομαι"): "did you become angry at, hate," governing dative οἱ ("him"). The speaker questions why Zeus was so wrathful toward someone in broad Troy.

lines.original: τέκνον ἐμόν, ποῖόν σε ἔπος φύγεν ἕρκος ὀδόντων.
lines.english: My child, what sort of word has escaped the barrier of your teeth?
lines.gloss: **τέκνον** (n. nom./voc. sg., "child") **ἐμόν** (adj. nom./voc. sg., "my"), **ποῖόν** (interrog. adj. acc. sg., "what kind of"), **φύγεν** (aor. ind. act. 3rd sg. φεύγω, "escaped"), **ἕρκος ὀδόντων** (acc. sg. + gen. pl., "barrier of teeth," i.e., lips). Zeus addresses Athena with the affectionate vocative "my child," then asks rhetorically "what kind of word escaped the barrier of your teeth," a formulaic expression for speaking ill-advisedly or surprisingly.

lines.original: πῶς ἂν ἔπειτʼ Ὀδυσῆος ἐγὼ θείοιο λαθοίμην,
lines.english: How could I then forget godlike Odysseus,
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** πῶς (adv.) "how?"; λαθοίμην (aor. opt. mid., 1st sg. of λανθάνω) "could I forget" (+ gen.); Ὀδυσῆος (gen. sg.) "of Odysseus"; θείοιο (gen. sg. adj.) "divine, godlike"; ἂν (particle) with optative expressing potential mood.

Athena asks rhetorically "How could I ever forget godlike Odysseus?", with the potential optative construction (ἂν + optative) emphasizing the impossibility of such forgetfulness.

lines.original: ὃς περὶ μὲν νόον ἐστὶ βροτῶν, περὶ δʼ ἱρὰ θεοῖσιν
lines.english: He surpasses mortals in wisdom and in sacred offerings to the immortal gods.
lines.gloss: **ὃς** (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) "who" – refers to Odysseus; **περὶ** (adverb) "exceedingly, above" – used twice for emphasis; **νόον** (noun, acc. sg. masc.) "in mind/intelligence"; **βροτῶν** (noun, gen. pl. masc.) "of mortals"; **ἱρὰ** (noun, acc. pl. neut.) "sacrifices, sacred offerings"; **θεοῖσιν** (noun, dat. pl. masc.) "to the gods." Athena praises Odysseus as surpassing mortals in intelligence and gods in sacrificial offerings.

lines.original: ἀθανάτοισιν ἔδωκε, τοὶ οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἔχουσιν;
lines.english: he has given to the immortal gods who hold broad heaven?
lines.gloss:
**ἀθανάτοισιν** (adj. dat. pl. masc.) "to the immortals" - dative of indirect object with ἔδωκε. **ἔδωκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of δίδωμι) "gave, has given" - main verb governing the dative. **τοί** (rel. pron. nom. pl. masc.) "who" - refers back to ἀθανάτοισιν. **οὐρανὸν εὐρύν** (acc. sg. masc.) "broad heaven" - direct object of ἔχουσιν. **ἔχουσιν** (3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of ἔχω) "hold, possess" - defines the immortals as heaven-dwellers.

The line completes the rheto

lines.original: ἀλλὰ Ποσειδάων γαιήοχος ἀσκελὲς αἰεὶ
lines.english: But Poseidon the earth-shaker relentlessly always
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλὰ Ποσειδάων γαιήοχος ἀσκελὲς αἰεὶ**

*ἀλλὰ* (conjunction): "but" – strong adversative marking contrast. *Ποσειδάων* (nom. sg.): Poseidon, subject of the implicit verb of anger. *γαιήοχος* (nom. sg. epithet): "earth-shaker," traditional epithet for Poseidon. *ἀσκελὲς* (adv.): "unceasingly, relentlessly." *αἰεὶ* (adv.): "always, ever." The line emphasizes Poseidon's continuous, unrelenting wrath against Odysseus.

lines.original: Κύκλωπος κεχόλωται, ὃν ὀφθαλμοῦ ἀλάωσεν,
lines.english: He rages at the Cyclops whose eye he blinded.
lines.gloss:
**Κύκλωπος κεχόλωται, ὃν ὀφθαλμοῦ ἀλάωσεν,**

Κύκλωπος (genitive singular of Κύκλωψ) "of the Cyclops"; κεχόλωται (perfect middle/passive indicative, 3rd singular of χολόομαι) "is enraged"; ὃν (accusative singular masculine relative pronoun) "whom"; ὀφθαλμοῦ (genitive singular of ὀφθαλμός) "of his eye" (genitive of separation); ἀλάωσεν (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular of ἀλαόω) "he blinded." Poseidon remains enraged on behalf of the Cyclops Polyphemus, whom Odysseus depr

lines.original: ἀντίθεον Πολύφημον, ὅου κράτος ἐστὶ μέγιστον
lines.english: godlike Polyphemos, whose strength is greatest of all
lines.gloss:
**ἀντίθεον Πολύφημον, ὅου κράτος ἐστὶ μέγιστον**

*ἀντίθεον* (adj., acc. sg. masc.) "godlike, rivaling the gods" modifies Polyphemus; *Πολύφημον* (proper noun, acc. sg.) "Polyphemus," object identifying the specific Cyclops; *κράτος* (noun, nom. sg. neut.) "power, might"; *μέγιστον* (adj., nom. sg. neut., superlative) "greatest, mightiest." The line emphasizes Polyphemus's divine-like status and supreme power among all the Cyclopes.

lines.original: πᾶσιν Κυκλώπεσσι· Θόωσα δέ μιν τέκε νύμφη,
lines.english: among all the Cyclopes; and the nymph Thoosa bore him,
lines.gloss: **πᾶσιν Κυκλώπεσσι·** πᾶσιν (dat. pl. masc. of πᾶς, "all") with Κυκλώπεσσι (dat. pl., "among the Cyclopes") — "among all the Cyclopes"; **Θόωσα** (nom. sg. fem., "Thoosa," the nymph's name); **τέκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of τίκτω, "bore, gave birth to"); **μιν** (acc. sg., enclitic pronoun, "him"); **νύμφη** (nom. sg. fem., "nymph, maiden"). The verse states that the nymph Thoosa bore him (Polyphemus), whose power is greatest among all the Cyclopes.

lines.original: Φόρκυνος θυγάτηρ ἁλὸς ἀτρυγέτοιο μέδοντος,
lines.english: daughter of Phorcys who rules over the barren sea
lines.gloss:
**Φόρκυνος** (gen. sg. of Φόρκυς): "of Phorcys," genitive of possession modifying "daughter." **θυγάτηρ** (nom. sg.): "daughter," subject in apposition to Thoosa. **ἁλὸς ἀτρυγέτοιο** (gen. sg.): "of the barren/unharvested sea," genitive governed by μέδοντος. **μέδοντος** (pres. part. gen. sg. of μέδω): "ruling (over)," masculine participle agreeing with Φόρκυνος, governing the genitive ἁλός.

Thoosa is identified as daughter of Phorcys, who rules over the barren sea—a genealogical detail explaining Poseidon's connection to the Cyclops Polyphemus.

lines.original: ἐν σπέσσι γλαφυροῖσι Ποσειδάωνι μιγεῖσα.
lines.english: in hollow caves having lain with Poseidon.
lines.gloss:
**ἐν σπέσσι γλαφυροῖσι Ποσειδάωνι μιγεῖσα.**

Key words: **σπέσσι** (noun, dative plural of σπέος) "in caves"; **γλαφυροῖσι** (adjective, dative plural) "hollow, deep"; **Ποσειδάωνι** (proper noun, dative singular) "with Poseidon"; **μιγεῖσα** (participle, aorist passive, nominative singular feminine of μίγνυμι) "having mingled with, having had intercourse with." Thoosa, daughter of Phorcys, united with Poseidon in hollow caves.

lines.original: ἐκ τοῦ δὴ Ὀδυσῆα Ποσειδάων ἐνοσίχθων
lines.english: From that time Poseidon the earth-shaker has pursued Odysseus
lines.gloss: **ἐκ** (prep. + gen.): "from" or "because of," governing **τοῦ** (demonstrative pronoun, gen. sing. neut.): "that [incident]," referring to the blinding of Polyphemus. **Ὀδυσῆα** (acc. sing.): Odysseus, object of the verb. **Ποσειδάων** (nom. sing.): Poseidon, subject. **ἐνοσίχθων** (nom. sing., epithet): "earth-shaker," in apposition to Poseidon. "From that [incident] then, Poseidon the earth-shaker [persecutes] Odysseus"—establishing the divine wrath as the primary obstacle to his homecoming.

lines.original: οὔ τι κατακτείνει, πλάζει δʼ ἀπὸ πατρίδος αἴης.
lines.english: He does not kill him outright, but drives him wandering far from his native land.
lines.gloss:
**κατακτείνει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of κατα-κτείνω): "kill outright, slay." **πλάζει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of πλάζω): "drives off course, causes to wander." **πατρίδος** (gen. sg. fem. of πατρίς): "fatherland, native land" (gen. of separation). **αἴης** (gen. sg. fem. of αἶα): "land, earth" (in apposition to πατρίδος). 

Athena notes that Poseidon does not kill Odysseus outright but rather drives him away from his homeland, emphasizing the god's strategy of prolonged suffering through wandering rather than direct destruction.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἄγεθʼ, ἡμεῖς οἵδε περιφραζώμεθα πάντες
lines.english: But come now, let us all here consider together
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλά** (ἀλλʼ): strong adversative conjunction, "but, come now." **ἄγε** (ἄγεθʼ): 2nd plural present imperative of ἄγω, "come!" (exhortation). **περιφραζώμεθα**: 1st plural present middle subjunctive of περιφράζομαι, "let us consider, devise." **πάντες**: nominative plural masculine of πᾶς, "all (of us)."

Athena (or another deity) urges the assembled gods to deliberate together about Odysseus's return, using the hortatory subjunctive to propose collective action.

lines.original: νόστον, ὅπως ἔλθῃσι· Ποσειδάων δὲ μεθήσει
lines.english: Let us all consider his homecoming, how he may return, and Poseidon will let go his wrath.
lines.gloss:
**νόστον, ὅπως ἔλθῃσι· Ποσειδάων δὲ μεθήσει**

**νόστον** (acc. sing. masc., "return, homecoming") — object of περιφραζώμεθα from the previous line; **ὅπως** (conjunction, "how, in what way") with **ἔλθῃσι** (3rd sing. aor. subj. of ἔρχομαι, "he may come") forms a purpose/deliberative clause; **Ποσειδάων** (nom. sing., "Poseidon") subject; **μεθήσει** (3rd sing. fut. of μεθίημι, "will let go, relent"). The gods deliberate Odysseus's return, suggesting that Poseidon will abandon his hostility.

lines.original: ὃν χόλον· οὐ μὲν γάρ τι δυνήσεται ἀντία πάντων
lines.english: He will let go his anger, for he will not be able to contend alone against all the immortal gods.
lines.gloss:
**ὃν χόλον· οὐ μὲν γάρ τι δυνήσεται ἀντία πάντων**

Key words: **ὃν** (relative pronoun, accusative singular masculine) "his/which"; **χόλον** (noun, accusative singular) "wrath, anger"; **δυνήσεται** (verb, future middle/passive 3rd singular of δύναμαι) "he will be able"; **ἀντία** (preposition + genitive or adverb) "against, in opposition to"; **πάντων** (adjective, genitive plural masculine) "of all."

Athena assures that Poseidon will release his wrath, for he will not be able (to strive) alone against all the other immortal gods.

lines.original: ἀθανάτων ἀέκητι θεῶν ἐριδαινέμεν οἶος.
lines.english: For he will not be able alone to contend against the will of all the immortal gods.
lines.gloss: **ἀθανάτων** (gen. pl. of ἀθάνατος): "of the immortal [gods]," genitive of separation with ἀέκητι. **ἀέκητι** (dat. sg. of ἀέκητι, adverbial): "against the will," governing genitive. **θεῶν** (gen. pl. of θεός): "of the gods," in apposition to ἀθανάτων. **ἐριδαινέμεν** (pres. inf. of ἐριδαίνω): "to contend, to strive," complementary infinitive. **οἶος** (nom. sg. masc. of οἶος): "alone," in apposition to the subject. The line states that he will not be able to contend alone against the will of the immortal gods.

lines.original: ὦ πάτερ ἡμέτερε Κρονίδη, ὕπατε κρειόντων,
lines.english: O our father, son of Kronos, highest of all rulers,
lines.gloss: **ὦ** (vocative particle) introduces direct address; **πάτερ** (voc. sg. of πατήρ) "father"; **ἡμέτερε** (voc. sg. masc. of ἡμέτερος) "our"; **Κρονίδη** (voc. sg. of Κρονίδης) "son of Kronos," epithet of Zeus; **ὕπατε** (voc. sg. of ὕπατος) "highest"; **κρειόντων** (gen. pl. of κρείων) "of rulers/lords." Athena addresses Zeus with a series of formal epithets: "O our father, son of Kronos, highest of rulers."

lines.original: εἰ μὲν δὴ νῦν τοῦτο φίλον μακάρεσσι θεοῖσιν,
lines.english: If indeed this is now pleasing to the blessed gods
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *εἰ* (conjunction) "if" introduces a conditional clause; *μὲν δή* (particles) combine for emphasis "indeed now"; *τοῦτο* (demonstrative pronoun, nominative neuter singular) "this thing," referring to Odysseus's return; *φίλον* (adjective, nominative neuter singular) "dear, pleasing"; *μακάρεσσι θεοῖσιν* (adjective + noun, dative plural) "to the blessed gods." 

Athena presents a conditional statement: "If indeed this thing is now pleasing to the blessed gods," setting up her appeal regarding Odysseus's homecoming.

lines.original: νοστῆσαι Ὀδυσῆα πολύφρονα ὅνδε δόμονδε,
lines.english: for resourceful Odysseus to return to his own home
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** νοστῆσαι (aorist infinitive of νοστέω, "to return home"), Ὀδυσῆα (accusative singular of Ὀδυσσεύς, "Odysseus"), πολύφρονα (accusative singular masculine of πολύφρων, "much-thinking, resourceful"), δόμονδε (adverb, "homeward, to one's home"). 

The line presents the infinitive clause completing the conditional from the previous verse: "for much-thinking Odysseus to return home here," with πολύφρονα as a typical epithet emphasizing Odysseus's cleverness and δόμονδε reinforcing the goal of homecoming.

lines.original: Ἑρμείαν μὲν ἔπειτα διάκτορον ἀργεϊφόντην
lines.english: Then we shall urge Hermes the messenger, slayer of Argus
lines.gloss:
**Ἑρμείαν μὲν ἔπειτα διάκτορον ἀργεϊφόντην**

Ἑρμείαν: accusative singular of Ἑρμείας, "Hermes" (direct object). διάκτορον: accusative singular masculine of διάκτορος, "messenger, guide." ἀργεϊφόντην: accusative singular masculine of ἀργεϊφόντης, "slayer of Argus" (epithet of Hermes). The line identifies Hermes as the messenger whom the gods will send, with μὲν anticipating a following δέ construction and ἔπειτα marking the next step in the divine plan.

lines.original: νῆσον ἐς Ὠγυγίην ὀτρύνομεν, ὄφρα τάχιστα
lines.english: We will send the messenger Hermes to the island of Ogygia, so that as quickly as possible
lines.gloss: **νῆσον** (acc. sing. fem. of νῆσος): "island," object of ἐς, referring to Ogygia. **Ὠγυγίην** (acc. sing. fem. adj.): "Ogygian," modifying νῆσον. **ὀτρύνομεν** (1st pl. pres. indic. act. of ὀτρύνω): "we urge/hasten," the gods sending Hermes. **ὄφρα** (conj.): "in order that," introducing purpose clause. **τάχιστα** (adv. superlative): "most swiftly/as quickly as possible," modifying the subsequent action.

lines.original: νύμφῃ ἐυπλοκάμῳ εἴπῃ νημερτέα βουλήν,
lines.english: to tell the fair-tressed nymph our unerring counsel
lines.gloss:
**νύμφῃ** (noun, dative singular feminine) "to the nymph" - dative of indirect object with εἴπῃ. **εὐπλοκάμῳ** (adjective, dative singular feminine) "fair-tressed, with beautiful braids" - epithet modifying νύμφῃ, referring to Calypso. **εἴπῃ** (verb, 3rd singular aorist subjunctive active) "that he may tell" - purpose clause dependent on ὀτρύνομεν. **νημερτέα** (adjective, accusative singular feminine) "unerring, infallible, true" - modifying βουλήν. **βουλήν** (noun, accusative singular feminine) "plan, counsel, decree" - direct object of εἴπῃ.

The line means: "that he may tell the

lines.original: νόστον Ὀδυσσῆος ταλασίφρονος, ὥς κε νέηται·
lines.english: the return of stout-hearted Odysseus, so that he may come home.
lines.gloss:
**νόστον Ὀδυσσῆος ταλασίφρονος, ὥς κε νέηται·**

*νόστον* (acc. sg. masc., "return, homecoming") is the object of an implied verb of telling from the previous context. *Ὀδυσσῆος* (gen. sg., "of Odysseus") is a possessive genitive modifying νόστον. *ταλασίφρονος* (gen. sg. masc., "stout-hearted, enduring") is an epithet in apposition to Ὀδυσσῆος. *ὥς* ("so that") with *κε* (modal particle) and *νέηται* (3rd sg. pres. mid. subj. of νέομαι, "he may return") forms a purpose clause expressing the intention that Tel

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐγὼν Ἰθάκηνδʼ ἐσελεύσομαι, ὄφρα οἱ υἱὸν
lines.english: But I will go to Ithaca, so that I may rouse his son.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἐγὼν (ἐγώ): first person singular pronoun, nominative, "I." Ἰθάκηνδε (Ἰθάκην + -δε): accusative with directional suffix, "to Ithaca." ἐσελεύσομαι (εἰσ-έρχομαι): first person singular future middle indicative, "I will go into/enter." ὄφρα: conjunction with subjunctive, "in order that, so that." υἱόν: accusative singular masculine of υἱός, "son."

Athena declares her intention to travel to Ithaca to rouse Odysseus' son to action.

lines.original: μᾶλλον ἐποτρύνω καί οἱ μένος ἐν φρεσὶ θείω,
lines.english: I will urge on his son more strongly and put courage in his heart,
lines.gloss:
**μᾶλλον** (adverb): "more, rather" – intensifies the verb ἐποτρύνω.

**ἐποτρύνω** (1st sg. fut. act. indic., from ἐποτρύνω): "I will urge on, incite" – primary verb expressing encouragement of Telemachus.

**μένος** (neut. acc. sg., from μένος): "spirit, courage, strength" – direct object of θείω.

**φρεσί** (fem. dat. pl., from φρήν): "in the heart/mind" – locative dative indicating where courage will be placed.

**θείω** (1st sg. fut. act. indic., from τίθημι): "I will place, put" – coordinated with ἐποτρύνω, expressing the goddess's intent to instill courage

lines.original: εἰς ἀγορὴν καλέσαντα κάρη κομόωντας Ἀχαιοὺς
lines.english: to call the long-haired Achaeans to assembly
lines.gloss: **Key words:** εἰς ἀγορήν (εἰς + acc., "into the assembly"), καλέσαντα (aor. act. ptc. acc. masc. sg. of καλέω, "having summoned"), κάρη κομόωντας (acc. masc. pl. ptc. of κομάω, "long-haired," epithet), Ἀχαιούς (acc. pl., "Achaeans/Greeks"). Telemachus is urged to call the long-haired Achaeans into assembly, using the traditional Homeric epithet for Greek warriors distinguished by their flowing hair.

lines.original: πᾶσι μνηστήρεσσιν ἀπειπέμεν, οἵ τέ οἱ αἰεὶ
lines.english: to declare to all the suitors who are always
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** πᾶσι (dative plural adjective from πᾶς, "to all"), μνηστήρεσσιν (dative plural noun, "to the suitors"), ἀπειπέμεν (aorist infinitive of ἀπεῖπον, "to renounce/forbid"), αἰεί (adverb, "always/continually"). 

The line expresses the purpose "to renounce/forbid all the suitors, who always..." with the dative μνηστήρεσσιν as object of the compound verb ἀπειπέμεν.

lines.original: μῆλʼ ἁδινὰ σφάζουσι καὶ εἰλίποδας ἕλικας βοῦς.
lines.english: who continually slaughter his crowding sheep and shambling crook-horned cattle.
lines.gloss: **μῆλα** (n. acc. pl., from μῆλον): "sheep/flocks," object of σφάζουσι. **ἁδινά** (adj. acc. pl. neut.): "abundant, thronging," modifying μῆλα. **σφάζουσι** (v. 3rd pl. pres. act. ind., from σφάζω): "they slaughter," main verb describing the suitors' ongoing consumption. **εἰλίποδας** (adj. acc. pl., from εἰλίπους): "rolling-gaited, shambling," epithet modifying βοῦς. **ἕλικας** (adj. acc. pl. f., from ἕλιξ): "curved-horned," additional epithet for βοῦς. **βοῦς** (n. acc. pl., from β

lines.original: πέμψω δʼ ἐς Σπάρτην τε καὶ ἐς Πύλον ἠμαθόεντα
lines.english: I will send you to Sparta and to sandy Pylos
lines.gloss:
**πέμψω** (fut. act. ind. 1st sg. of πέμπω) "I will send"; **Σπάρτην** (acc. sg. fem.) "to Sparta"; **Πύλον** (acc. sg. masc.) "to Pylos"; **ἠμαθόεντα** (acc. sg. masc. adj.) "sandy." 

Athena announces her intention to send Telemachus on his journey to the two major destinations, with the epithet "sandy" characterizing Pylos by its coastal location.

lines.original: νόστον πευσόμενον πατρὸς φίλου, ἤν που ἀκούσῃ,
lines.english: to inquire about the return of my dear father, if I might hear something somewhere,
lines.gloss: **νόστον** (acc. sg. masc., "return/homecoming") is the object of πευσόμενον; **πευσόμενον** (fut. mid. participle of πυνθάνομαι, "to inquire about/learn of") expresses purpose; **πατρὸς φίλου** (gen. sg., "of his dear father") is an objective genitive dependent on νόστον; **ἀκούσῃ** (3rd sg. aor. subj. of ἀκούω, "he may hear") appears in an indefinite temporal clause with **ἤν που** ("if perhaps/anywhere"). The line explains Telemachus will travel to inquire about his father's return, in case he might hear news anywhere.

lines.original: ἠδʼ ἵνα μιν κλέος ἐσθλὸν ἐν ἀνθρώποισιν ἔχῃσιν.
lines.english: and so that he may have good repute among men.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *κλέος* (n. nom./acc. sg. neut.) "fame, glory"; *ἐσθλόν* (adj. nom./acc. sg. neut.) "good, noble"; *ἀνθρώποισιν* (n. dat. pl. masc.) "among men"; *ἔχῃσιν* (3rd sg. pres. subj. act., ἔχω) "he may have."

Telemachus's journey serves a dual purpose: not only to seek news of his father, but also so that he may win noble renown among mortals through this quest.

lines.original: χαῖρε, ξεῖνε, παρʼ ἄμμι φιλήσεαι· αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα
lines.english: Welcome, stranger, you shall be treated as a friend among us; but afterwards
lines.gloss: **χαῖρε** (verb, 2nd sg. pres. imperat. of χαίρω): "rejoice, hail, welcome"; **ξεῖνε** (noun, voc. sg. of ξεῖνος): "stranger, guest"; **φιλήσεαι** (verb, 2nd sg. fut. indic. pass. of φιλέω): "you will be treated as a friend, welcomed"; **ἔπειτα** (adverb): "afterwards, then." Nausicaa extends hospitality to Odysseus, promising he will be welcomed as a guest-friend, with details to follow after.

lines.original: δείπνου πασσάμενος μυθήσεαι ὅττεό σε χρή.
lines.english: After you have partaken of dinner you shall tell us what you need.
lines.gloss: **δείπνου** (genitive singular of δεῖπνον): "of dinner," partitive genitive with πασσάμενος; **πασσάμενος** (aorist middle participle, nominative singular masculine of πατέομαι): "having partaken of," "having eaten"; **μυθήσεαι** (future middle 2nd singular of μυθέομαι): "you will tell," "you will speak"; **ὅττεό** (genitive of relative pronoun ὅστις): "of what," "of the things which"; **χρή** (impersonal verb): "it is necessary." Nausicaa invites the stranger to speak after partaking of dinner, explaining what he needs.

lines.original: ξεῖνε φίλʼ, ἦ καί μοι νεμεσήσεαι ὅττι κεν εἴπω;
lines.english: Dear guest, will you hold it against me for what I am about to say?
lines.gloss:
**ξεῖνε** (voc. sg. m. of ξεῖνος): "guest, stranger" – vocative of address.
**φίλʼ** (voc. sg. m. of φίλος): "dear" – elided adjective modifying ξεῖνε.
**νεμεσήσεαι** (2nd sg. fut. mid. indic. of νεμεσάω): "you will be indignant, you will blame (me)" – future middle expressing taking offense.
**ὅττι κεν εἴπω** (relative clause with modal particle): "whatever I may say" – ὅττι (neut. acc. sg. of ὅστις), κεν (= ἄν), εἴπω (1st sg. aor. subj. of εἶπον/ἔπ

lines.original: τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή,
lines.english: These things are their concern, the lyre and song.
lines.gloss:
**τούτοισιν** (dat. pl. masc. of οὗτος): "for these men," dative of interest. **μέλει** (3rd sg. pres. ind. of μέλω): "is a care/concern," impersonal verb taking dative of person and nominative of thing. **κίθαρις** (nom. sg. fem.): "the lyre," subject of μέλει. **ἀοιδή** (nom. sg. fem.): "song," second subject coordinated with κίθαρις.

The line means "For these men the lyre and song are a concern/matter of interest," describing the suitors' carefree pursuits.

lines.original: ῥεῖʼ, ἐπεὶ ἀλλότριον βίοτον νήποινον ἔδουσιν,
lines.english: easily, since they devour another man's livelihood without paying penalty
lines.gloss:
**ῥεῖα** (adverb): "easily, without cost" - modifies the suitors' enjoyment of feasting. **ἀλλότριον** (adjective, masculine accusative singular): "belonging to another, someone else's" - modifies **βίοτον**. **βίοτον** (noun, masculine accusative singular): "livelihood, substance, property" - object of **ἔδουσιν**. **νήποινον** (adjective, masculine accusative singular): "without penalty, unavenged" - modifies **βίοτον**. **ἔδουσιν** (verb, 3rd person plural present active indicative of ἔδω): "they consume, devour."

The line explains why the suitors feast carelessly with music: they easily consume another man's property without paying compensation.

lines.original: ἀνέρος, οὗ δή που λεύκʼ ὀστέα πύθεται ὄμβρῳ
lines.english: A man whose white bones are rotting in the rain somewhere.
lines.gloss: **ἀνέρος** (gen. sg. of ἀνήρ, "of the man") is the genitive governed by **ὀστέα** ("bones," nom./acc. pl. neut. of ὀστέον). **λεύκʼ** (nom./acc. pl. neut. of λευκός, "white") modifies the bones. **πύθεται** (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass. of πύθω, "rot, decay") describes the bones' decomposition. **ὄμβρῳ** (dat. sg. of ὄμβρος, "by rain/storm") indicates the instrumental cause of decay.

lines.original: κείμενʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείρου, ἢ εἰν ἁλὶ κῦμα κυλίνδει.
lines.english: lying on the mainland, or the waves roll them in the sea.
lines.gloss:
**κείμενʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείρου, ἢ εἰν ἁλὶ κῦμα κυλίνδει.**

**κείμενα** (pres. mid./pass. participle of κεῖμαι, "lying"): modifies "white bones" from the previous line, describing them lying on land. **ἠπείρου** (gen. sg. of ἤπειρος, "mainland, shore"): location where the bones lie. **ἁλί** (dat. sg. of ἅλς, "sea"): alternative location introduced by **ἢ** ("or"). **κῦμα** (nom. sg., "wave"): subject of κυλίνδει. **κυλίνδει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of κ

lines.original: εἰ κεῖνόν γʼ Ἰθάκηνδε ἰδοίατο νοστήσαντα,
lines.english: If they should see that man returning home to Ithaca
lines.gloss:
**εἰ κεῖνόν γʼ Ἰθάκηνδε ἰδοίατο νοστήσαντα**

*εἰ* (conditional particle) "if"; *κεῖνον* (demonstrative pronoun, acc. sg. masc.) "that man," = *ἐκεῖνον*, referring to Odysseus; *Ἰθάκηνδε* (adverb with directional suffix -δε) "to Ithaca"; *ἰδοίατο* (3rd pl. aorist optative middle of ὁράω) "they would see"; *νοστήσαντα* (aorist participle acc. sg. masc. of νοστέω) "having returned." The suitors would wish to be swifter of foot if they saw him returned to Ithaca

lines.original: πάντες κʼ ἀρησαίατʼ ἐλαφρότεροι πόδας εἶναι
lines.english: They would all pray to be swifter of foot rather than richer in gold and clothing.
lines.gloss:
**πάντες** (nom. pl. masc., πᾶς): "all," subject of ἀρησαίατο. **ἀρησαίατο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. opt., ἀράομαι): "they would pray (for)," expressing a wish or potential action. **ἐλαφρότεροι** (nom. pl. masc. comparative, ἐλαφρός): "swifter, lighter," predicate adjective modifying πόδας. **πόδας** (acc. pl. masc., πούς): "in feet," accusative of respect. **εἶναι** (pres. inf., εἰμί): "to be," completing the indirect statement after ἀρησαίατο.

The line means "all would pray to be swifter of foot," expressing the suitors' hypothetical wish

lines.original: ἢ ἀφνειότεροι χρυσοῖό τε ἐσθῆτός τε.
lines.english: than richer in gold and clothing.
lines.gloss:
**ἢ** (conj.): "or" (alternative to previous wish about being swifter-footed)
**ἀφνειότεροι** (adj., nom. pl. masc., comparative of ἀφνειός): "richer, wealthier"
**χρυσοῖο** (noun, gen. sg. masc.): "in gold" (genitive of specification)
**ἐσθῆτός** (noun, gen. sg. fem.): "in clothing" (genitive of specification)

The speaker presents an alternative wish: that all would pray to be richer in gold and clothing rather than swifter of foot.

lines.original: νῦν δʼ ὁ μὲν ὣς ἀπόλωλε κακὸν μόρον, οὐδέ τις ἡμῖν
lines.english: But now he has perished in an evil fate, and there is no comfort for us.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ὁ μέν (pronoun, nominative singular masculine) "he" – refers to Odysseus; ἀπόλωλε (verb, perfect indicative active, 3rd singular, from ἀπόλλυμι) "has perished"; κακὸν μόρον (noun phrase, accusative singular) "an evil fate/death" – accusative of manner; ἡμῖν (pronoun, dative plural) "for us." 

Penelope laments that Odysseus has perished by an evil fate, leaving them (her and Telemachus) without comfort or hope.

lines.original: θαλπωρή, εἴ πέρ τις ἐπιχθονίων ἀνθρώπων
lines.english: There is no comfort for us, even if some mortal man should say he will return.
lines.gloss:
**θαλπωρή** (nom. sg. fem. noun) "warmth, comfort, consolation"; **εἴ πέρ** (conditional particle + intensive particle) "even if"; **ἐπιχθονίων** (gen. pl. masc. adj.) "of earthly, of those upon the earth," modifying **ἀνθρώπων** (gen. pl. masc. noun) "of men, of humans." 

Penelope declares there is no comfort (for her), even if any earthly person should say Odysseus will return.

lines.original: φῇσιν ἐλεύσεσθαι· τοῦ δʼ ὤλετο νόστιμον ἦμαρ.
lines.english: She says he will return, but his day of homecoming has perished.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** φῇσιν (3rd sg. pres. indic. of φημί, "he says/claims"), ἐλεύσεσθαι (fut. infin. of ἔρχομαι, "to come/will come"), ὤλετο (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ὄλλυμι, "perished, was destroyed"), νόστιμον (adj. acc. sg. neut., "of homecoming"), ἦμαρ (acc. sg. neut., "day"). 

Someone claims that he will come, but his day of homecoming has perished—a report of return contradicted by the grim reality that the homecoming is already lost.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἄγε μοι τόδε εἰπὲ καὶ ἀτρεκέως κατάλεξον·
lines.english: But come now, tell me this and relate it truthfully:
lines.gloss:
**ἄγε** (verb, 2nd sg. imperative of ἄγω) "come now," an interjection used to introduce a request. **τόδε** (pronoun, neut. acc. sg. of ὅδε) "this thing," direct object of εἰπέ. **εἰπέ** (verb, 2nd sg. aorist imperative of εἶπον/λέγω) "tell, say." **ἀτρεκέως** (adverb) "exactly, truthfully, accurately." **κατάλεξον** (verb, 2nd sg. aorist imperative of καταλέγω) "recount, relate in detail."

The speaker urges: "But come, tell me this and recount it accurately," introducing a request for truthful information.

lines.original: τίς πόθεν εἰς ἀνδρῶν; πόθι τοι πόλις ἠδὲ τοκῆες;
lines.english: Who are you and where are you from among men, and where are your city and parents?
lines.gloss: **τίς** (interrogative pronoun, nominative singular) "who"; **πόθεν** (interrogative adverb) "from where"; **ἀνδρῶν** (noun, genitive plural of ἀνήρ) "of men"; **πόθι** (interrogative adverb, enclitic) "where"; **τοκῆες** (noun, nominative plural of τοκεύς) "parents." Odysseus asks the stranger's identity and origin: "Who are you, from where among men? Where are your city and parents?"

lines.original: ὁπποίης τʼ ἐπὶ νηὸς ἀφίκεο· πῶς δέ σε ναῦται
lines.english: On what sort of ship did you arrive, and how did the sailors
lines.gloss:
**ὁπποίης** (interrogative adjective, genitive singular feminine) "of what kind," modifying νηός. **ἐπί** (preposition + genitive) "on, upon." **νηός** (noun, genitive singular feminine) "ship." **ἀφίκεο** (2nd singular aorist middle indicative of ἀφικνέομαι) "did you arrive, come." **ναῦται** (noun, nominative plural masculine) "sailors." 

Odysseus asks: "On what kind of ship did you arrive? And how did the sailors bring you?"

lines.original: ἤγαγον εἰς Ἰθάκην; τίνες ἔμμεναι εὐχετόωντο;
lines.english: They brought you to Ithaca? Who did they claim to be?
lines.gloss: **ἤγαγον** (ἄγω, 2nd aor. act. ind. 3rd pl.): "they brought" – the sailors conducted you. **Ἰθάκην** (acc. sing.): "to Ithaca" – destination of the voyage. **τίνες** (interrog. pron. nom. pl.): "who?" – asking the identity of the sailors. **ἔμμεναι** (εἰμί, pres. inf.): "to be" – in indirect statement. **εὐχετόωντο** (εὐχετάομαι, imperf. mid. ind. 3rd pl.): "they claimed/professed" – they boasted or declared themselves to be.

lines.original: οὐ μὲν γάρ τί σε πεζὸν ὀίομαι ἐνθάδʼ ἱκέσθαι.
lines.english: For I do not think you came here on foot.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** πεζόν (adjective, masculine accusative singular) "on foot"; ὀίομαι (verb, 1st singular present middle/passive indicative) "I think, suppose"; ἐνθάδε (adverb) "here, to this place"; ἱκέσθαι (verb, 2nd aorist middle infinitive of ἱκνέομαι) "to come, arrive."

The speaker declares "For I do not think that you came here on foot," implying the stranger must have arrived by ship and thus suspecting his identity or connection to seafarers.

lines.original: καί μοι τοῦτʼ ἀγόρευσον ἐτήτυμον, ὄφρʼ ἐὺ εἰδῶ,
lines.english: And tell me this truthfully, so that I may know well,
lines.gloss:
**Target line glossing:**

**τοῦτο** (demonstrative pronoun, neuter accusative singular) "this" – object of ἀγόρευσον; **ἀγόρευσον** (aorist imperative active, 2nd singular of ἀγορεύω) "tell, speak"; **ἐτήτυμον** (adjective, neuter accusative singular) "truly, truthfully" – modifying τοῦτο; **ὄφρα** (conjunction) "so that, in order that" – introducing purpose clause; **εἰδῶ** (1st singular perfect subjunctive active of οἶδα) "I may know."

The speaker requests truthful information ("tell me this truly") with a purpose clause expressing the desired result of knowing well.

lines.original: ἠὲ νέον μεθέπεις ἦ καὶ πατρώιός ἐσσι
lines.english: Are you a new friend or were you also a guest-friend of my father?
lines.gloss: **ἠέ** (conj.): "or," introducing an alternative question. **νέον** (adv.): "recently, newly," modifying μεθέπεις. **μεθέπεις** (2nd sg. pres. indic. of μετέπω): "you pursue, you seek out," indicating recent acquaintance. **πατρώιος** (adj., nom. sg. masc.): "ancestral, hereditary," predicate describing a long-standing guest-friendship. **ἐσσι** (2nd sg. pres. indic. of εἰμί): "you are." Telemachus asks whether Odysseus is a new acquaintance or an ancestral guest-friend of his father.

lines.original: ξεῖνος, ἐπεὶ πολλοὶ ἴσαν ἀνέρες ἡμέτερον δῶ
lines.english: A guest-friend, since many men used to come to our house.
lines.gloss: **ξεῖνος** (noun, nom. sg.) "guest-friend, stranger" - subject of an implied verb; **πολλοί** (adj., nom. pl. masc.) "many" modifying **ἀνέρες** (noun, nom. pl.) "men"; **ἴσαν** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. of εἶμι) "came, went"; **ἡμέτερον** (possessive adj., acc. sg. neut.) "our" modifying **δῶ** (noun, acc. sg., Doric for δῶμα) "house, dwelling." The speaker asks if the visitor is a guest-friend, noting that many men used to come to their house (likely referring to Odysseus's hospitable nature).

lines.original: ἄλλοι, ἐπεὶ καὶ κεῖνος ἐπίστροφος ἦν ἀνθρώπων.
lines.english: Various men came to our house, since he too was hospitable to people.
lines.gloss: **ἄλλοι** (nom. pl. masc., ἄλλος): "others," "other men" - contrasting with the previous suitors mentioned. **ἐπεί**: causal conjunction, "since" or "because." **κεῖνος** (nom. sg. masc., κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος): "that man," referring to Odysseus. **ἐπίστροφος** (nom. sg. masc.): "skilled in turning," "cunning," "clever" - describing Odysseus's characteristic intelligence. **ἀνθρώπων** (gen. pl., ἄνθρωπος): "among men" or "of men," genitive of comparison/sphere. The line explains that there were other suitors since Odysseus himself was a man of exceptional cunning.

lines.original: τοιγὰρ ἐγώ τοι ταῦτα μάλʼ ἀτρεκέως ἀγορεύσω.
lines.english: Therefore I will speak these things to you very truthfully.
lines.gloss: **τοιγάρ** (inferential particle): "therefore, so then" – marks a logical conclusion. **ἐγώ** (personal pronoun, nominative): "I" – emphatic first-person subject. **ταῦτα** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative neuter plural): "these things" – direct object of ἀγορεύσω. **ἀτρεκέως** (adverb): "accurately, truthfully" – modifies ἀγορεύσω. **ἀγορεύσω** (verb, future 1st singular, from ἀγορεύω): "I will tell/declare." Athena (disguised as Mentes) promises to speak truthfully about the matters at hand.

lines.original: Μέντης Ἀγχιάλοιο δαΐφρονος εὔχομαι εἶναι
lines.english: I claim to be Mentes, son of wise Anchialus, and I rule over the oar-loving Taphians.
lines.gloss: **Μέντης** (nom. sg. masc.) "Mentes" – proper name, subject of εὔχομαι. **Ἀγχιάλοιο** (gen. sg. masc.) "of Anchialus" – patronymic genitive depending on υἱός (in next line). **δαΐφρονος** (gen. sg. masc.) "warlike, skilled in battle" – epithet modifying Ἀγχιάλοιο. **εὔχομαι** (1st sg. pres. mid. indic.) "I claim, boast" – main verb. **εἶναι** (pres. act. infin.) "to be" – complementary infinitive with εὔχομαι. Athena (disguised) claims to be Mentes, son of warlike Anchialus.

lines.original: υἱός, ἀτὰρ Ταφίοισι φιληρέτμοισιν ἀνάσσω.
lines.english: I am his son, and I rule over the Taphians who love their oars.
lines.gloss:
**υἱός** (noun, nominative singular masculine) "son" – in apposition to Μέντης, completing Athena's false identity claim.

**ἀτάρ** (particle) "but, moreover" – transitional conjunction adding further detail.

**Ταφίοισι** (noun, dative plural masculine) "over the Taphians" – ethnic name, governed by ἀνάσσω.

**φιληρέτμοισιν** (adjective, dative plural masculine) "oar-loving" – compound epithet modifying Ταφίοισι, emphasizing their seafaring nature.

**ἀνάσσω** (verb, first person singular present active indicative) "I rule, I am lord" – completes Athena's claim to be chieftain of the Taphians.

lines.original: νῦν δʼ ὧδε ξὺν νηὶ κατήλυθον ἠδʼ ἑτάροισιν
lines.english: Now I have come here thus with my ship and companions
lines.gloss: **νῦν** (adverb): "now"; **ξὺν νηΐ** (preposition + dative singular of ναῦς): "with (my) ship"; **κατήλυθον** (1st singular aorist indicative of κατέρχομαι): "I have come down, I have arrived"; **ἑτάροισιν** (dative plural of ἑταῖρος): "with (my) companions." Athena (disguised as Mentes) describes her current arrival by ship with her crew, continuing her fabricated travel narrative.

lines.original: πλέων ἐπὶ οἴνοπα πόντον ἐπʼ ἀλλοθρόους ἀνθρώπους,
lines.english: sailing over the wine-dark sea to men of foreign speech
lines.gloss:
**πλέων** (pres. act. participle, nom. sg. masc. of πλέω): "sailing"
**οἴνοπα** (acc. sg. masc. of οἶνοψ): "wine-dark" (epithet modifying πόντον)
**πόντον** (acc. sg. masc. of πόντος): "sea"
**ἀλλοθρόους** (acc. pl. masc. of ἀλλόθροος): "foreign-speaking, of alien speech"

The speaker describes sailing over the wine-dark sea toward people of foreign speech, continuing the journey motif from the previous line's reference to arriving by ship with companions.

lines.original: ἐς Τεμέσην μετὰ χαλκόν, ἄγω δʼ αἴθωνα σίδηρον.
lines.english: To Temese for bronze, and I bring gleaming iron.
lines.gloss:
**ἐς** (preposition + acc.): "to, toward" — governing Τεμέσην. **Τεμέσην** (acc. sg. fem. proper noun): Temese, a trading port associated with copper. **χαλκόν** (acc. sg. masc.): "bronze" or "copper" — object of pursuit/exchange. **ἄγω** (1st sg. pres. act. indic.): "I bring, I carry." **σίδηρον** (acc. sg. masc.): "iron" — the cargo being transported for trade.

The speaker explains his mercantile voyage to Temese in search of copper, while bringing iron as trade goods.

lines.original: νηῦς δέ μοι ἥδʼ ἕστηκεν ἐπʼ ἀγροῦ νόσφι πόληος,
lines.english: My ship stands here in the country away from the city, in Rheithron harbor beneath wooded Neion.
lines.gloss: **νηῦς** (noun, nom. sg. fem.) "ship" — subject of the sentence. **ἕστηκεν** (verb, 3rd sg. perfect active indic. of ἵστημι) "stands, is stationed" — perfect denoting present state. **ἐπʼ ἀγροῦ** (prep. + gen. sg. masc.) "at the field, by the countryside" — locative expression. **νόσφι** (prep. + gen.) "apart from, away from" — with **πόληος** (gen. sg. fem. of πόλις) "the city." The speaker explains that his ship is moored in the countryside away from the town.

lines.original: ἐν λιμένι Ῥείθρῳ ὑπὸ Νηίῳ ὑλήεντι.
lines.english: in the harbor Rheithron below wooded Neion.
lines.gloss:
**ἐν λιμένι Ῥείθρῳ ὑπὸ Νηίῳ ὑλήεντι.**

Key words: **ἐν** (preposition + dative) "in"; **λιμένι** (noun, dative singular) "harbor"; **Ῥείθρῳ** (proper noun, dative singular) "Rheithron" (harbor name); **Νηίῳ** (proper noun/adjective, dative singular) "Neion" (mountain name); **ὑλήεντι** (adjective, dative singular) "wooded, forested." The ship is located in the harbor called Rheithron beneath wooded Mount Neion.

lines.original: ξεῖνοι δʼ ἀλλήλων πατρώιοι εὐχόμεθʼ εἶναι
lines.english: We claim to be guest-friends of one another from our fathers' time.
lines.gloss: **ξεῖνοι** (nom. pl. masc., *ξεῖνος*): "guest-friends, hereditary friends" - subject of the infinitive *εἶναι*. **ἀλλήλων** (gen. pl., reciprocal pronoun): "of one another, of each other" - modifying *πατρώιοι*. **πατρώιοι** (nom. pl. masc., *πατρῷος*): "ancestral, inherited from our fathers" - predicate adjective describing the nature of the guest-friendship. **εὐχόμεθʼ** (1st pl. pres. mid. indic., *εὔχομαι*): "we boast, we claim" - main verb. **εἶναι** (pres. inf., *εἰμί*): "to be" - completing the indirect

lines.original: ἐξ ἀρχῆς, εἴ πέρ τε γέροντʼ εἴρηαι ἐπελθὼν
lines.english: from the beginning, if you should go and question the old man
lines.gloss: ἐξ ἀρχῆς (prep. + gen.): "from the beginning," marking temporal starting point. εἴ πέρ τε (conditional particle + emphatic particle + enclitic particle): "if indeed," strengthening the conditional. γέροντ(α) (acc. sg. masc., γέρων): "old man," direct object of εἴρηαι. εἴρηαι (2nd sg. aor. mid. subj., εἴρομαι): "you should ask." ἐπελθών (aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. masc., ἐπέρχομαι): "going to (him), approaching." The speaker invites inquiry about their guest-friendship from the beginning, if the addressee should visit and question the old man.

lines.original: Λαέρτην ἥρωα, τὸν οὐκέτι φασὶ πόλινδε
lines.english: the hero Laertes, who they say no longer comes to the city
lines.gloss: **Λαέρτην** (acc. sg. masc., proper name) "Laertes," object of εἴρηαι; **ἥρωα** (acc. sg. masc., noun) "the hero," in apposition to Λαέρτην; **οὐκέτι** (adverb) "no longer"; **φασὶ** (3rd pl. pres. act. indic., φημί) "they say"; **πόλινδε** (adverb) "to the city," indicating direction. The line introduces Laertes as one who, people say, no longer comes to the city.

lines.original: ἔρχεσθʼ, ἀλλʼ ἀπάνευθεν ἐπʼ ἀγροῦ πήματα πάσχειν
lines.english: come, but far off in the countryside to suffer sorrows
lines.gloss:
**ἔρχεσθ'** (ἔρχεσθαι), present middle/passive infinitive of ἔρχομαι, "to come/go." **ἀπάνευθεν**, adverb with genitive, "far from, away from." **ἀγροῦ**, genitive singular of ἀγρός, "field, farm" (dependent on ἀπάνευθεν). **πήματα**, accusative plural neuter of πῆμα, "suffering, woe." **πάσχειν**, present active infinitive of πάσχω, "to suffer, endure."

The line describes Laertes' condition: he no longer comes to town but remains far from it on his farm, enduring sufferings.

lines.original: γρηὶ σὺν ἀμφιπόλῳ, ἥ οἱ βρῶσίν τε πόσιν τε
lines.english: with an old serving woman who provides him food and drink
lines.gloss:
**γρηὶ** (noun, dative singular feminine from γρηῦς): "with an old woman" - dative of accompaniment.

**ἀμφιπόλῳ** (noun, dative singular feminine from ἀμφίπολος): "servant, attendant" - in apposition to γρηΐ, describing her role.

**βρῶσίν** (noun, accusative singular feminine from βρῶσις): "food" - direct object of the implied verb of giving.

**πόσιν** (noun, accusative singular masculine from πόσις): "drink" - paired with βρῶσίν as objects.

The line describes Laertes attended by an old serving woman who provides him with food and drink.

lines.original: παρτιθεῖ, εὖτʼ ἄν μιν κάματος κατὰ γυῖα λάβῃσιν
lines.english: who serves him food and drink whenever weariness seizes his limbs
lines.gloss:
**παρτιθεῖ** (παρατίθημι): 3rd sg. pres. act. indic., "sets before (him)," referring to the old serving woman providing food and drink. **εὖτʼ ἄν**: temporal conjunction with modal particle, "whenever" (with subjunctive, creating a general temporal clause). **κάματος**: nom. sg. masc., "weariness, fatigue." **γυῖα**: acc. pl. neut. (γυῖον), "limbs." **λάβῃσιν**: 3rd sg. aor. act. subj. (λαμβάνω), "seizes, takes hold of."

The verse describes the servant setting out provisions whenever fatigue overtakes Laertes' limbs.

lines.original: ἑρπύζοντʼ ἀνὰ γουνὸν ἀλωῆς οἰνοπέδοιο.
lines.english: crawling about over the ridges of his vineyard.
lines.gloss: **ἑρπύζοντα** (ἕρπω, present participle, accusative singular masculine) "crawling, creeping" – describes Odysseus moving slowly; **ἀνά** (preposition + accusative) "up along, throughout"; **γουνόν** (γουνός, accusative singular masculine) "plot, field"; **ἀλωῆς** (ἀλωή, genitive singular feminine) "vineyard, orchard"; **οἰνοπέδοιο** (οἰνόπεδον, genitive singular neuter) "of the vine-planted (land), of the vineyard." The line depicts Odysseus crawling through the terraced vineyard plot, emphasizing his exhausted, laborious movement.

lines.original: νῦν δʼ ἦλθον· δὴ γάρ μιν ἔφαντʼ ἐπιδήμιον εἶναι,
lines.english: But now I have come, for people said that he was home, your father.
lines.gloss:
**νῦν δʼ ἦλθον· δὴ γάρ μιν ἔφαντʼ ἐπιδήμιον εἶναι,**

**νῦν** (adverb): "now"; **ἦλθον** (1st sg. aorist indicative of ἔρχομαι): "I came"; **ἔφαντʼ** (3rd pl. imperfect of φημί, elided before ἐπιδήμιον): "they said/declared"; **ἐπιδήμιον** (accusative masc. sg. adjective): "in the land, at home"; **εἶναι** (present infinitive of εἰμί): "to be." The speaker explains their arrival, stating they came because people said he (Odysseus) was at home.

lines.original: σὸν πατέρʼ· ἀλλά νυ τόν γε θεοὶ βλάπτουσι κελεύθου.
lines.english: Your father, but the gods are blocking his path.
lines.gloss: **σὸν** (possessive adj., acc. sing. masc.) "your" - modifying πατέρα. **πατέρʼ(α)** (noun, acc. sing.) "father" - object of implied verb of seeking/finding. **θεοὶ** (noun, nom. pl.) "the gods" - subject of βλάπτουσι. **βλάπτουσι** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. act. indic. of βλάπτω) "hinder, obstruct" - main verb. **κελεύθου** (noun, gen. sing.) "from the path, journey" - genitive of separation with βλάπτουσι. Telemachus is told that his father still lives but the gods obstruct him from his homeward journey.

lines.original: οὐ γάρ πω τέθνηκεν ἐπὶ χθονὶ δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς,
lines.english: For godlike Odysseus has not yet perished upon the earth.
lines.gloss:
**οὐ γάρ πω τέθνηκεν ἐπὶ χθον�ὶ δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς**
